Live Trading Floor with Craig Tapping - Friday AM

Hosted by Craig Tapping | Friday 30 October 2026
https://academy.masteringthemarkets.com/c/mtm-upcoming-events/live-trading-floor-with-craig-tapping-friday-am-083a07 ↗
Bullish Setups: Oil, TLT / US Bonds, XEJ (Energy), Financials / Banks, Industrials, A-REITs (SCG, SGP, GPT, VCX, MGR, CHC), GMG, STO, WDS, Refiners (ALD, VEA), APA, NXT, CDA, LOV, GNC, PME, SHL, RHC, BXB, QAN, ACL, AUZ, CBA, Sugar
Bearish Setups: S&P 500 / Nasdaq, Semiconductors (SOX), INTC, Gold, Silver / Platinum / Palladium, Copper / Industrial Metals, Iron ore & metal miners (CIA), XMJ (Materials), XSJ (Staples), Telecoms, COL, WOW, MP1, HVN, FPH, TLX, DXN, Wheat
Neutral / Watching: Bitcoin, Uranium, Lithium / Rare Earths, Natural Gas, Soybeans, Corn / TAGS (Agriculture), XJO, XHJ (Health Care), Utilities, AGL, XRO, WTC, PMV, EDV, A2M, TWE, MTS, ELD, CSL, RMD, COH, CPU, WOR, IXR, REH, ING
S&P 500 / Nasdaq Bearish TA 00:01:11
  • Earnings are the likely catalyst for a top: Q3 beat rates (first 24% of S&P reporting) fell to 83% EPS / 66% revenue, from 88% / 77% last quarter — revenue now below the multi-year average
  • Market priced for perfection: beats still punished (Intel −20%, Caterpillar −9.3% after hours); misses crushed (ServiceNow −27%, Google −12.5%, Robinhood −7%, Amazon −5.2%)
  • SPY/QQQ making higher highs on RSI bearish divergence and lower highs on OBV/volume since June — "our markets are fragile" (00:10:38)
  • US markets have gone nowhere since February; October recovery bounces in sectors are now rolling over (utilities, staples, energy, telcos)
  • Still defensive since mid-August; only short-term 3:1 trades, no swing trades or big positioning — risk/reward not in our favour late cycle
  • Fed held, but ~85% odds of a hike on 9 December — still a contraction phase
Semiconductors (SOX) Bearish TA 00:20:21
  • OBV led price in the Oct–Dec accumulation; smart money then took profits as volume stopped supporting the move
  • Second push was volume-supported but now selling off — losing the support level opens a broader sell-off
  • Overnight: AMD −6%, ARM −7%, Micron/TSMC/Broadcom −3%, Intel −23%; Dell/HP −4–7%; watch the KOSPI (SK Hynix/Samsung lead US semis by 1–2 days)
  • Revisited at 01:50:24: SOX closed ~513, trading ~485 after hours (−5.5%) → large gap down at the open
  • Won't short after a 5–6% gap — the stop must sit above the gap (R:R drops to ~2.2, much worse with a 3x leveraged bear ETF); a gap fill over the next week would be the time to short
INTC (Intel) Bearish TA 01:34:44
  • −22% after hours on earnings, from a close of ~$92 to ~$71
  • Up ~650% on the "Trump pump"; could fully reverse to the pre-announcement level around ~$48–50
  • "Be very careful"
TLT / US Bonds Bullish TA 01:44:40
  • US yields fell hard this week (10Y back to ~4.9%); the market went from pricing 3 more Fed hikes to 2
  • Bought TLT at $76, now ~$81; could still put in one more low, but the low may already be in — the biggest bond bounce all year
  • Money rotating into bonds = de-risking out of equities — initially bearish for stocks and metals, long-term healthy (yields fall → money later rotates back into stocks)
  • AU yields also falling (2Y still pricing ~1 hike); if the RBA doesn't hike next week that would be a bullish surprise for markets
Gold Bearish TA 00:24:33
  • Small bounce ($4,000 → $4,070) mostly reversed to ~$4,015; hidden bearish divergence — "the pressure is down"
  • Key low to protect: $3,942 — above it, the triangle (or W-X-ABC) still allows a recovery bounce before more downside; below it, straight into further decline
  • Expected more of a recovery after a ~$700 fall from ~$4,700; precious metals need a proper change of structure in gold first
Silver / Platinum / Palladium Bearish TA 00:26:35
  • Silver: continuous lower lows and lower highs, can't get a recovery bounce — "on a big decline"
  • Platinum and silver have both lost their lows; palladium didn't even bounce
  • No buying support at all; not expecting success in other precious metals until gold changes structure
Copper / Industrial Metals Bearish TA 00:28:40
  • Strong Tuesday/Wednesday, then a "diabolical" Thursday sell-off; zinc, nickel and tin also selling, aluminium holding better
  • Copper ending diagonal — potential ~15% pullback over the coming months, with other industrial metals following (01:33:42)
Iron ore & metal miners (CIA) Bearish TA 01:33:42
  • "Hard to be bullish on metals right now" — heavy selling pressure
  • Iron ore underperforming (not enough construction demand); steel holding up better
  • Iron is approaching the next key level where buyers might step in, but there's no reason to buy producers while expecting deeper corrections
Uranium Neutral TA 00:29:11
  • Uranium spot had its biggest daily gain since February while everything else sold off — worth watching
  • Equities are still trading risk-off and not following the commodity
  • Equities are back toward the commodity price, as in April 2023 / April 2025 (both followed by good moves) — risk/reward getting attractive, but they can still go lower
Lithium / Rare Earths Neutral TA 00:46:42
  • Lithium: spodumene down ~50% over 4 months and not bouncing, plus poor risk sentiment — needs one or both to change
  • Rare earths are also sentiment-driven; both are in the retracement zone but still dragged down by risk-off sentiment
Oil Bullish TA 00:30:12
  • Holding up; Netanyahu's election win reduces the odds of Middle East de-escalation; midterms on 3 November still to come
  • Still looking for higher oil prices; a pullback was anticipated first
Natural Gas Neutral TA 00:31:44
  • Seasonally its time of year, but nothing yet — sold off then rebounded; chatter about a mild winter
  • Needs a break above ~$3.30 to confirm
Soybeans Neutral TA 01:11:59
  • At previous highs/resistance on declining volume; hidden bull divergence now
  • Expects one more high into resistance on bearish divergence, then a bigger pullback, then later continuation
Wheat Bearish TA 01:13:31
  • "Smashed" — fell out of the channel; very close to breaking structure
  • Taking out the low ends any bullish structure — the ABC would be complete and you'd wait for a new base
Sugar Bullish TA 01:14:01
  • Still constructive — multiple 1-2s now playing out as 4-5s; potentially two more moves up before a correction
Corn / TAGS (Agriculture) Neutral TA 01:14:34
  • Corn "obliterated" alongside wheat; TAGS in an ABC with C ≈ A — potentially a low soon
  • RSI fully reset, strong hidden bullish divergence across corn, wheat and TAGS — potential good setups after softs ran hard
  • Too soon — wait for buyers to step in first
  • Softs had a small bounce this week (the only green sector) — needs follow-through (00:32:15)
Bitcoin Neutral TA 00:32:45
  • Selling off aggressively after the expected wave 2 back-test of the 50-day MA; a ~$5.6B Binance hack added fear
  • Bullish scenario: big reaction at ~$73k (200-day MA ~$73,118 plus the long-liquidation pool at $73–75k) → wave 3 up
  • Lose $73k and drop quickly → bearish: fair-value gap / 0.786 at ~$66–67.5k, larger liquidity below, likely new lows for BTC and alts (01:22:16)
  • Alternate count: expanded-flat ABC (B wave) with the C wave still to come; tech sell-off correlation matters
XJO (ASX 200) Neutral TA 00:34:49
  • Strong green opening candle today; ASX has had no clear direction all year
XEJ (Energy) Bullish TA 00:35:22
  • Energy up nicely; the expected pullback depended on oil pulling back — if that doesn't happen, energy goes again
  • Could break the resistance in place since March and take out the March high
XMJ (Materials) Bearish TA 00:36:23
  • Bounced into previous support, now resistance, and battling to break out as precious metals fail to attract buyers
  • Only had this as a wave 4 bounce before a wave 5 to complete the correction
Financials / Banks Bullish TA 00:37:24
  • Still climbing (~10% recovery bounce in October)
  • Tighten stops and lock in profits ahead of Tuesday's RBA decision — a hike would pressure banks; falling yields may be what's lifting them (01:46:14)
XHJ (Health Care) Neutral TA 00:38:24
  • Still pushing up in wave 5, close to his ~37,100 target (~5% upside)
  • Momentum starting to stall — "the pointy end of the stick"; a bigger wave 2 pullback follows
XSJ (Staples) Bearish TA 00:39:24
  • "Absolutely smashed" today, bucking the market — driven by the heavily weighted Coles result; expanded flat breaking down (01:06:44)
Utilities Neutral TA 00:39:55
  • Nearing the top of the channel where it has always been rejected — protect trades rather than add risk
Industrials Bullish TA 00:40:26
  • Performing well this month; potentially breaking through the level
Telecoms Bearish TA 00:40:26
  • Hasn't broken the key S/R zone or the trend line — bias still to the downside; "still a little concerned"
Refiners (ALD, VEA) Bullish TA 00:41:30
  • Had the pullbacks he wanted, now bouncing; still bullish on refineries long term
  • Caution: in a 3-4 / 3-4 chop zone that could last until about Q2 next year before the bigger expansion
APA Bullish TA 00:42:32
  • Nice breakout this week; utilities overall near the top of the channel, so be careful

Session Themes

  • Earnings cracks are the potential catalyst for a market top: falling beat rates, and even beats being sold off — a market priced for perfection, late cycle, still in a tightening/contraction phase
  • Breadth/volume warning: higher highs on lower OBV and RSI divergence across SPY, QQQ and SOX; October recovery bounces now rolling over — stay defensive, short-term 3:1 trades only
  • Bonds catching their biggest bid of the year — money de-risking out of equities into bonds, initially bearish for stocks/metals but healthy long-term; falling yields may take pressure off an RBA hike (no hike = bullish surprise)
  • Metals weak across the board (gold must hold $3,942; silver/PGMs/copper/iron failing); energy, refiners, REITs and selected healthcare/industrials the relative strength on the ASX
  • Gap-trading lesson: don't chase a short after a 5–6% gap down — the stop has to cover a gap fill, which destroys R:R (worse with leveraged ETFs); wait for the fill
  • Don't buy the 5th wave — wait for the wave 2 pullback (REH, GNC, WOW); marking a level isn't a buy signal — wait for buyers to confirm (uranium, softs)
  • Head-and-shoulders credibility depends on the slope (horizontal or sloping in the breakout direction)

Session Themes

  • Backtest every indicator yourself before trusting social-media claims — for silver, weekly bull divergence and dips under the 200-week MA have a much better track record than "RSI oversold" or a stochastic reset
  • Know what a signal "owes" you: hourly divergence = an hourly bounce, weekly divergence = months of turnaround — don't expect a major bottom from a lower-timeframe signal
  • Execute on your own rules even when respected educators disagree (CBA vs Shane's count); it's fine to be in a trade you don't think is the major bottom as long as risk/reward is right
  • Don't buy directly under major resistance or before the first S/R flip; many stocks are pumping into resistance after heavy falls (relief rallies) — expect some to roll over
  • High-risk "banger" trades (NXT-style breakaway gaps) only with small capital and a defined stop; adapting your theory as new data arrives is for experienced traders — beginners should hold their stops
  • Park idle capital in slow movers (CBA, Telstra) and swap out quickly for higher-probability setups
  • Midterms approaching and markets shaky — be careful, take stops, protect capital

Session Themes

  • The Fed held (10–2, hawkish tone) as fully priced in; inflation is reaccelerating in both headline and core — ~77–85% odds of a December hike, ~40% for another in January; PCE tonight and US jobs next Friday are key
  • Australia's inflation is the bigger problem — an RBA hike on Cup Day is ~85–90% priced, which is negative for small caps and rate-sensitive sectors and supportive for the AUD
  • Hormuz closure is the swing factor for oil, inflation and yields; the oil Elliott count still targets above $120
  • Earnings season: EPS beats strong, revenue beats weak; the market demands perfection late in the cycle (Alphabet −10%); forward P/Es are not stretched
  • Capital rotation: tech hardware → software, mega caps → Dow/Russell/defensives — money is rotating, not leaving the market
  • COT: institutions backing the Russell, bonds and gold; reducing exposure to silver, the Dow, copper, the Nikkei and the AUD
  • Psychology: 2026 has been the hardest trading year since 2007 — not a reflection of students' ability; keep marking up charts ("prepare for the harvest") and wait for confirmed reactions
  • Cycles: AI is in the Perez "invention" phase near a 2000-style top; expects a 2027 bear market, a 3–4 year bull market, and a final low around 2032; next week's call is a cycles deep dive (K-wave, Perez, Benner, 18.6-year property cycle) instead of the usual review
  • Calendar: ECB and BoJ decisions (holds expected — a hike would shock markets), Eli Lilly/Amazon/Chevron/Exxon earnings, US midterms Tuesday 3 Nov (a Democrat sweep could move markets), RBA on Cup Day

Session Themes

  • Not a trending market: buy capitulation and extreme fear on oversold blinkers (low volume plus bullish divergence), sell into euphoria at the zag zone / resistance — 'rinse and repeat'
  • Exhaustion gaps and breakaway gaps are his two favourite gap setups (NXT breakaway; URNM/WOR/BAP/WIRE exhaustion) — covered in next week's year-long course module
  • Using ETFs (URNM, lithium ETF, WIRE, GDX, VSO) to play sector bounces without single-stock risk; larger sizing (~5%) on ETFs vs 2–2.5% on stocks
  • Separate accounts for separate purposes: trade the bounce in the trading account while DCAing long-term — removes the FOMO of selling
  • Exit when the reasons change (AGL, NIC): small losses are fine, big losses aren't; you can always buy back later (BIO)
  • Precious and base metals at major supports with capitulation sentiment; watch silver at the zag zone as the trigger for the whole complex

DTR (Dateline Resources) Neutral FA 00:03:00
  • Up about 25% on no news, with volume. A member asked about it over the weekend.
  • The Colosseum gold/rare earths project has been stalled since August by a court action from a conservation group.
  • DTR has appealed. The US Department of Justice and Department of War have filed separately too, because they see the project as nationally significant.
  • The filings went in at the end of September. Buying today may mean something is moving in the courts, but there are no dates or visibility.
  • Craig: "I don't have a bearing either way." Follow the story. A continued stall would hold up a high-profile project the US government cares about.
IPT (Impact Minerals) Neutral FA 00:05:50
  • Also up about 25%. Has gone in and out of favour with the HPA (high purity alumina) story.
  • The strategic reset Craig wanted has happened: the 80%-held HPA unit is now the primary focus. He says that should have happened long ago.
  • PFS from about a year ago: IRR 47%, NPV over A$1B (capex needed). Craig hasn't reviewed the PFS in over a year.
  • Has a stake in a competitor, held purely as an investment.
  • Key watch item: the pilot plant. Equipment delivery and installation have started, and flowsheet validation or strong recoveries would be potential catalysts.
  • Few pure HPA options exist, so it will keep getting attention if management stays focused.
TUA (Tuas) Bearish FA 00:08:58
  • Teaching point on "TA in a vacuum": after the earlier big gap down, members kept sending charts expecting a bounce and gap fill. Craig said all along to leave it alone.
  • It has gapped down again on heavy volume. The Singapore regulator (IMDA) has issued subsidiary Simba Telecom a show-cause notice.
  • Allegations: using spectrum it wasn't allocated, prohibited spectrum sharing, breaching production orders, and governance and compliance-culture failures over several years.
  • The serious potential penalties are suspension or cancellation of spectrum rights and cancellation of licences, which could end the business.
  • Not found guilty yet, but the IMDA wouldn't issue the notice without strong justification. The response is due 16 November.
  • "Stay well away" until there is real information suggesting the charges will go away. Note: Craig's last FA entry was Bullish (27 Jul FA + TA, before the regulatory problems). Today's view is clearly bearish.
STK (Strickland Metals) Neutral FA 00:15:19
  • Fell sharply on no real news. The speeding-ticket response pointed to elections in the host country (Serbia). Jurisdiction and election risk is a Fund 101 lesson.
  • Craig has long called it significantly overvalued. Market cap has dropped from about $600-700M to about $150M, so "now it's time to have it on our list."
  • Global resource is about 9-10Moz gold equivalent. Rudnik is the higher-grade deposit at about 1.8Moz at 2.8 g/t. The other deposits are lower-grade gold that relies on Cu/Ag/Zn/Pb credits, and one has about 5Moz.
  • Zijin Mining (the biggest miner in Serbia) and Jupiter hold stakes. Cash isn't an issue.
  • The weakness is that there is still no economic study showing how they would mine these grades. The PFS depends on a drill program still to come. Management is "really slow," so expect a long time lag.
RAP (Resolution Minerals) Neutral FA 00:19:38
  • A member favourite since Craig flagged it at a $15-20M market cap with defined copper resources, which protect the downside.
  • Market cap has fallen to about $10-11M, which makes it more attractive.
  • Re-assaying historic core with modern methods is giving strong results, e.g. ~2.14% Cu, 28m @ 1.67%, 32m @ 1.38%. Zinc and silver (polymetallic) are appearing too, which old models didn't include.
  • About $400-500k of non-dilutive cash from selling shares in another company puts the bank at about $1.8M. Spending is low, so the cap raise Craig was waiting on for entry may be further away.
  • Next steps: final assays from the last 3 historic holes, then an updated MRE. Craig would rather the raise came before the MRE update. Timing is unclear (4-12 weeks), and the quarterly should help.
  • "Still super interesting." The thesis is strengthening (undervaluation plus exploration catalyst), but he is still deciding how to play the entry.

PPL (Pureprofile) Bullish FA 00:29:54

LOT (Lotus Resources) Neutral FA 00:35:49
  • Question from Boyd. Shipping/export permits are finally approved, so product can move to port, including under-spec product from ramp-up.
  • It's progress, but not a sign the worst is over and not proof that ramp-up will succeed.
  • Market cap is about $90M against a $60M entitlement offer and $30M of convertibles. Port access may unlock a prepayment facility of up to $30M, which would give cash above market cap.
  • Risks: power disruptions (running on generators until the mains connection), and the acid plant at only about 50% capacity, which caps mining at about 50% too.

  • "Never take a position in ramp up." Wait for strong evidence the acid plant issues are behind them. The market cap means it has to be watched, carefully.

  • Question from Jeremy. The administrators are seeking up to 3 months' extension.
  • Recap: the Phase 3 trial was stopped as futile. Large amounts of data were missing, almost all from US sites. The company says the intact data looks positive.
  • Craig sees the extension as a good thing for holders. It gives time to assess the board-led recapitalisation proposal and other parties' proposals, finish the administrators' investigation, and get independent analysis of the Phase 3 results.
  • He expects it to be granted, since the alternative is likely the shares being deemed worthless (he has received that letter himself before).
  • Key watch item: whether the independent review matches the company's claims. If it does, there's an argument for redoing the trial and the asset keeps its value.
BHM (Broken Hill Mines) Bullish FA 00:47:01
  • Question from Kieran about the quarterly operations update. "Doing very, very well," exactly what Craig wanted.
  • Record silver production. Plant utilisation is 69%, the highest since June 2020. New mining areas are coming online to push towards nameplate.
  • The tailings dewatering plant, the key infrastructure for expansion, is on budget and on schedule for 1H CY27. The recent large cap raise funds it.
  • Ore sources: Pinnacles open pit, main lode underground at Rasp, and Rasp western area. Centenary is a significant growth area recently proven up by drilling.
  • Mainly zinc and silver exposure, with copper and gold credits in the lead concentrate.
  • Executing on time and on budget, the same quality as POL. Next: see the new areas embedded in the mine plan and get a tailings update.
IXC (Invex Therapeutics, ticker as transcribed) Neutral FA 00:49:54
  • Luke's pick-up. Market cap about $8M. Acquiring NZ company Recoba Therapeutics, which is repurposing nalfurafine (currently approved as an anti-itch drug) for demyelination in MS.
  • Preclinical data suggests it pushes immature cells to mature and remyelinate nerves, which would be repair rather than just slowing progression. It worked across animal models.
  • Plans a Phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (REVIVE) in relapsing-remitting MS. The existing safety data lets it go straight into a serious trial.
  • Light acquisition structure (shares plus 3 classes of milestone performance rights). Raising about $1M (firm commitments at $0.08) plus a $9.1M placement, about $10M in total, which is more than the market cap.
  • Concern: almost no information has been released (no presentation or trial design detail), which is "bizarre."
  • "One of the more interesting acquisitions I've seen in a long time." On the radar; Craig wants more information.
EXR (Elixir Energy) Neutral FA 00:56:09
  • Deal with Beach Energy (BPT) signed 23 Oct, after the earlier deadline passed with other parties circling.
  • Headline value about A$205M: about $25M cash plus about $180M of carried appraisal drilling and geotech/geophysical work. BPT farms into 50% of most assets over a 4-year funding pathway.
  • The $180M carry is EXR's $90M share plus BPT's own $90M. EXR keeps full interest in one project.
  • It validates EXR's work, since Beach is committing before the gas well results are complete.
  • A "no brainer" to accept because gas is long and expensive. Craig doesn't understand the earlier hesitation.
  • The market reaction was weaker than people expected. Craig calls it a fair, decent deal. Next: watch how quickly Beach moves on the Taroom Trough.

Session Themes

  • Context plus TA: TUA shows that charts read "in a vacuum" (gap-fill hopes) fail when the fundamental story is broken (regulatory licence risk). Know why a stock gapped before trading it.
  • Never take a position during ramp-up (LOT). Wait for strong evidence that operational issues are fixed, even when market cap looks cheap.
  • Falling valuations are bringing previously overvalued names (STK) and existing watchlist names (RAP, LOT) into "time to watch" territory.
  • Jurisdiction and election risk matters for offshore projects (STK/Serbia), a Fund 101 lesson.
  • Producers executing on plan (POL, BHM) look mispriced when the market misreads planned weak quarters.
  • Know the business stage (PPL): margin expansion on the cusp of consistent profitability is the interesting phase.
  • Cap raise timing as an entry tool, and how non-dilutive funding can delay it (RAP).

CYM is behind on the same oxide-to-sulphide pathway. Its edge is a clearer sulphide resource under the pit, but that doesn't justify a $90M market cap gap.

AEU (Atomic Eagle, ticker as transcribed) Bullish FA 00:53:00
  • Update requested by members. Nigeria project: one of the largest and highest-grade uranium resources globally, long sought after by majors.

  • Late September: a review to increase scale, change the mining inventory, enhance economics and update uranium price assumptions.

ADD (Adavale Resources) Bullish FA 00:59:15
  • The resource catalyst was played earlier. The stock then came back, and a $4.5M cap raise was done at 3c (price now a bit above).
  • Market cap only about $13-14M, with nearly 400koz of resource, $4.5M+ cash, a working mill on the edge of the pit, and permits to mine and process.
  • Resource growth is easy (almost every hole under the pit hit gold). The ground south and at depth was never mined. Higher-grade zones sit under the $4,200 pit shell, against an average of about 0.8-0.9g/t.
  • Consolidated tenure along the Parkes thrust near Northparkes, Cowal, McPhillamys, Evolution, Alkane and Fortescue. Alkane gave them some land and sits on the register.
  • Craig is most interested in drilling at Summers (looks very like London Victoria), Victoria South and Armstrong.
  • Scoping study on restarting production due in November is the next significant catalyst. "Definitely go and check them out." See the FA in Practice replay with Alan and David.

Session Themes

  • The small-cap sell-off is bargain-hunting season: prices people wished for are here. Build thesis and charts now, manage risk, execute when rules are met. A "healthy zag" on a multi-year view.
  • Read substantial holder notices properly: direct vs indirect vs convertibles/options. In large caps, big money cycles shares and lends for shorts, so notices can mislead TA readers.
  • Use broker flow and short-interest data (DYL) to see who is actually buying and selling.
  • Relative valuation between peers on the same pathway (CYM vs AR1) shows when a stock is overpriced.
  • Contract price lag (YAL) can signal next quarter's cash build ahead of time.
  • Early explorers: judge them by what they plan next (proper drill campaigns leading to a maiden MRE) and be wary of seasonal dead time (MHC winter shutdown).
  • No thesis change just because the share price fell (AEU, ADD). Falling prices can increase the value on offer.

France / French Government Bonds (OATs) Bearish Macro 00:00:42
  • Deep dive using the PESTLE model: Paris riots began as student protests over school funding, morphed into cost-of-living protests, then rioting and looting (150+ police injured, 1,000+ arrests; a centuries-old city hall burned)
  • Fiscal picture: deficit ~5.1% of GDP (2025), debt-to-GDP ~115–120%, government spending ~57% of GDP → a small, anaemic, over-taxed private sector

  • 10-year borrowing cost ~4.9% (versus sub-2% pre-COVID); France now pays a wider spread over German Bunds than Greece or Spain — bond vigilantes are voting with their feet
  • Not a reserve-currency issuer, so unlike the US it can't export its money printing; generous entitlements (30 days' leave, 35-hour week, near-free health care and education) aren't affordable at this debt load
  • ~7M people (13%) face food insecurity; youth unemployment is high; looting targeted groceries and luxury stores (Robin Hood / Arab Spring 2011 food-inflation parallels)

Session Themes

  • Tech-led US sell-off driven by AI growth concerns and central-bank tightening; the KOSPI, SOX and DRAM sitting on support are the three charts that decide the market
  • Big-picture cycle lens: AI hardware looks like a March 2000-style blow-off of the accumulation phase — a deep reset now, decades of upside after; at late-cycle tops, risk is high and reward is low
  • Always hold alternate bull/bear counts with clear invalidation and confirmation (S&P 7,500/7,860, gold 3,940, BTC $75k, oil $110/$90)
  • Oil is the macro swing factor: above $110–114 → a multi-month bear market across assets; below $90 → bullish for gold, crypto and stocks
  • Rate-hike contraction phase: own mega/large caps and defensives (staples, healthcare, utilities); small/micro caps get crushed until rate cuts are in view
  • Confirmation over anticipation: levels are areas of interest, not entries — wait for buyers to commit, a change of market structure and a weekly-close follow-through (TLX case study)
  • DCA only on the way up after a change of market structure; size falling-knife trades tiny (NXT)
  • Weekly candle review every Monday (evening stars, bearish engulfing) is one of the most valuable habits

ODY Neutral FA 00:24:15

BTR (Brightstar Resources) Neutral FA 00:28:41
  • Member asked whether the latest drilling announcement is grade smearing
  • The 305m intercept is hard to smear — it shows broad mineralisation, which is normal and fine for a nuggety/chunky gold deposit
  • But the shorter included intercepts are clearly smeared: 1m @ 8.72 g/t, ~9–10 g/t, 13.4 g/t and 59 g/t sections are propping up the 6–65m averages
  • Hit gold outside the existing MRE, so the resource will probably get bigger
  • Key concern: the grade at that depth is beyond open-pit reach but not good enough for underground
  • Mining through high- versus low-grade zones changes waste ratios, recoveries and revenue — these can be traded around once it's near production
  • Lookup sanity check: the prior FA entry (3 Feb 2026 FA Scan) was also Neutral — consistent
X2M Bullish FA 00:35:37
  • Very small cap (~$10–15M market cap) in data centres; strategy is regional sites with less power pressure, partnering with developers who add their own power
  • New binding deal: a ~$250M data-centre project; X2M manages the build/operations on a cost-plus basis, so the project value flows through as revenue with its cut as margin
  • Phased: it starts at 2.5MW (current grid connection), and the developer builds the extra 7.5MW to reach 10MW; running into 2028
  • Two binding deals now plus a ~200MW non-binding pipeline — "a really great announcement" and "a pretty big start" for such a small company
  • Now it has to deliver, or it'll be kicked out of the industry quickly; it is also raising capital
  • Lookup: no prior FA entry
AVE (Avecho) Neutral FA 00:39:18
  • "Last man standing" in cannabinoids for insomnia — every other CBD/sleep trial has failed against placebo
  • Uses a bioavailability-enhancing mechanism; spent years designing a very specific, well-targeted Phase 3 using competitors' failures, with two dose levels plus placebo
  • Data monitoring committee unblinded the interim data and recommended continuing unchanged (same dosing and patient numbers) — a good endorsement, but no guarantee of success
  • Recruitment has restarted for the final stage; readout timing is uncertain (could be 1–4 months after dosing ends)
  • If positive: a significant re-rate and a fast TGA pathway; potential partners are likely waiting for the result
  • It has run hard on the interim news — he'd prefer it pulls back to reduce downside before any position; still a binary outcome
  • Lookup sanity check: the prior FA entry (22 May 2026 FAQ Fridays) was also Neutral — consistent, though today's tone on trial quality is more constructive

Session Themes

  • Commodity research: "days of supply left" in exchange warehouses is a red herring on its own — compare it with the long-run average, and focus on the sustained gap between drawdown and replenishment
  • Small caps versus large caps: small caps are more volatile (thin liquidity, no big-money churn); swing trading under ~$1B market cap is hard, so you trade catalysts and stage/phase moments instead
  • Investing means accepting round trips: if you can't tolerate giving back gains over a 3–5 year horizon, use a "ride to fair value, exit, re-enter" strategy; value plays don't have to be held forever
  • Psychology: hold while the thesis holds; exit when the thesis, a stop or the timeframe breaks (ODY example); don't marry stocks; FA leads, TA can end a trade
  • Grade smearing: easy over short intercepts, hard over long ones — strip out the high-grade metre to see the real grade
  • Tranches in raises and debt facilities: shareholder votes, lapse risk, overhang, revenue-gated debt draws and lender warrants all change what a headline funding number really means
  • Graphite/HPA/rare earths downstream plays have very long qualification timelines — assume years
  • Next week: Tuesday calls are pre-recorded (Craig is at a Chilean mining-permitting lunch in Sydney)

Bearish Setups: US 10Y Yield, S&P 500 / Nasdaq, Bitcoin
Neutral / Watching: Oil (WTI), Gold
US 10Y Yield Bearish TA 00:03:09
  • 10Y pushed through 5% in late Sept to ~5.36%, the highest since 2002 (24-year high); now ~5.1% after a 15bp weekly drop, the biggest in ~7 months
  • Monthly bearish divergence + extremely overbought stochastic RSI — expects maybe one more spike (double top or marginal new high with divergence) then a multi-year retracement (0.333-0.666 of the 6-year advance from the 2020 low, possibly 2-3 years)
  • Fed funds 3.75-4% vs 2Y at 4.8% — an unusually wide gap last seen only in 1994-95; prior cycles saw the 10Y top near the Fed's peak rate
  • CME: ~93% hold at next week's FOMC; ~90% chance of at least one hike in December, ~41% chance of a second in January
  • Headline CPI 3.7% (vs 3.5% expected) but Cleveland Fed median CPI only 2.6% — inflation is energy-driven, which rate hikes can't fix (2020-22 "transitory" parallel)
  • Key difference this time: the Fed is restarting hikes rather than finished; yield curve still positive (not inverted); CAPE ~41, highest since 2000
TLT / US Bonds Bullish TA 00:11:31
  • TLT fell from ~$170 (2020) to a $76 low two weeks ago (>50% decline); now ~$80
  • Sell-off driven by central banks (notably China, Japan) dumping Treasuries for gold, plus investors preferring AI-driven equity gains
  • At 5-5.5% yields, bonds are becoming attractive vs a 1-1.5% S&P dividend with 20-30% downside risk
  • Monthly: deeply oversold, strong bullish divergence, buying volume arriving — no change of market structure yet
  • Potential recovery bounce to ~$110-130 (SAG zone) over the next few years; a divided Congress (less deficit spending) is a further tailwind for the long end
S&P 500 / Nasdaq Bearish TA 00:22:14
  • Every yield top since 1984 coincided with an S&P pullback as money rotated into bonds: 1984 -9%, 1987 -33%, 1994 -7%, 2000 -48%, 2007 -56%, 2011 -20%, 2018 -25%
  • Midterm seasonality is historically very bullish (Nov-Apr positive 18/18 times, ~15% average; 12 months after positive ~95%), but those stats are flattered by recoveries from big midterm-year crashes (1974, 2002, 2022) — this year indices are within ~1.5% of all-time highs, so there's no low base to recover from
  • Benner cycle peaks 2026; the 18.6-year cycle ends ~Oct 2027 (implied bottom); monthly market-cycle oscillator shows bearish divergence for only the 4th time in 60 years (1987, 2000, 2019, now) — expects a peak within 3-6 months, needing a catalyst
  • Republican president + Democratic Congress has been the weakest historical mix (~4.9% avg vs 12.9% for a full Republican sweep) — the most likely outcome (House flip ~90%, Senate ~60-63%)
  • Expect heavy volatility into the 3 Nov midterms; be careful trading the next 1.5 weeks
Oil (WTI) Neutral TA 00:10:44
  • The single deciding factor for risk assets after a yield top: oil kept running after 2000/2007 tops → everything sold off; oil rolled over in 1994/2018/2023 → markets rallied (2018 after an initial 2-3 month flush)
  • WTI ~$98 (Brent ~$110), up ~9% this month on the war — currently tracking the bearish ("red") template
  • Levels (WTI; add ~$10 for Brent): mid-range pivot $89-92 — back below it points to the bullish "green" path; war ceiling $100-114 — a push through it all but guarantees the red path (widening credit spreads, growth breaking)
  • Bear path 3: oil well over $100-114 and 10Y to 5.5-6% — only energy stocks would benefit
Gold Neutral TA 00:26:08
  • After yield tops gold fell 5 of 7 times (1984 -28%, 1987 -34%, 1994 -35%, 2000 -19%, 2007 -20%) but rallied in 2011 (+40%) and 2018 (+70%)
  • The difference was oil: when oil/CPI eased (2018, 2023), gold rallied (2023: ~$1,900 → $2,700, eventually ~$5,600)
  • Outcome depends on whether oil rolls over
Bitcoin Bearish TA 00:27:39
  • After yield tops: 2011 -94%, 2013 -86%; in 2018 it had already fallen 72%, people called the bottom, then it fell another 61% in 123 days before a 406% rally
  • Parallel to now: down ~53% from ATH with many calling the bottom at ~$57k
  • If oil keeps running (path 2), expects a market sell-off to drag crypto back to its lows or new lows before any recovery
  • Divided Congress makes crypto market-structure legislation (Clarity Act already failed) even harder; regulation shifts to the SEC; Democratic oversight likely to target World Liberty Financial / USD1 and the CZ pardon — headline risk for politically linked crypto

Session Themes

  • Yield tops tell you bonds have turned; oil tells you what risk assets do next — "seasonality is a tailwind, but rates and oil are the engine"
  • Three paths: (1) oil rolls over → bullish for stocks, gold, crypto; (2) oil keeps running → bonds rally, stocks/crypto sell off until demand breaks; (3) yields not done → 10Y to 5.5-6%, everything but energy suffers
  • Midterms: a House flip mostly means headlines and deadline fights; a Senate flip matters more (appointments incl. Fed nominees); gridlock limits new spending (good for bonds), but tariffs, trade, foreign policy (Iran/oil) and the Fed are unchanged
  • Checklist: FOMC next week (expect hold) → midterms 3 Nov → mid-Nov CPI/PPI (key for the December hike) → new Congress sworn in January → by January we'll know if yields have truly topped

Session Themes

  • Elliott Wave is about probabilities, not predictions: always run a bullish and a bearish scenario with clear invalidation, then react to the plan instead of panicking
  • Support/resistance is the foundation of TA (week 2 of the courses) — Russell, semis and DRAM all bounced exactly at major S/R levels
  • The October "green month" sector calls largely played out: energy, financials, discretionary, staples (+10%), utilities (+11%); only materials failed
  • Macro sequence: US yields topping → capital rotates into bonds (TLT at 24-year lows) → 3-6 months of weakness in stocks, crypto and metals → Bitcoin and gold lead the recovery; next gold/silver top ~2029-2030
  • US midterms (3 Nov) bring uncertainty — normally bearish into the vote, with recovery after; covered in tomorrow's macro call
  • Tech rotation, not a tech sell-off: hardware (semis/DRAM) is selling while software, cloud and cybersecurity hold up
  • Leveraged exposure via miners: miners outperform the commodity on the way up and fall harder on the way down — buy them after a sell-off, not after a catch-up run
  • Two types of correction: a pullback in price (PIP) vs. a pullback in time (PIT, sideways consolidation that resets momentum)
  • Long-term conviction: Amazon's -95% after the 2000 bubble preceded a ~101,000% gain; AI/robotics/automation is a two-decade generational-wealth play

Session Themes

  • Current regime: buy at extreme fear on key support, take profit into the zag zone and bank 3:1 trades — ride the structure only when it breaks through (e.g. XRO above the 0.618)
  • It's fine to exit and re-enter (COH, NXT, JHX, SLVM) — lock in gains when the reason for a trade disappears, and re-enter on better parameters
  • Smaller position sizes when entering without a change of market structure (NXG, SHL "being a bit naughty")
  • The energy bull market is the "obvious trade" no one is talking about (STO, WDS, XEJ through 12,000); look at higher timeframes so daily noise doesn't shake you out
  • Secular cycle thinking: CSL reset to 2015 levels was the buying opportunity; the Nasdaq is in an excess phase where long-term buyers risk giving back gains
  • "Show me the chart, I'll tell you the news" — bearish divergence and a change of structure often precede bad announcements (NXT, EIQ)
  • OBV across timeframes: look for confluence, but put the most weight on the daily (the most reliable in his backtesting)
  • Dividend-adjusted vs. unadjusted charts: chart unadjusted, check adjusted for high-yield stocks (WDS, FMG) since they can paint a very different trend picture
  • Risk management: high risk/reward setups (6:1) mean being right only 2-3 times out of 10 is profitable; avoid heavy debt when money isn't cheap

  • The deal is questionable. SPL took a controlling interest in the Italian therapeutics JV, while the bigger partner (Medici) handed over ~40% for just ~$3M cash plus ~$2M R&D support, despite an estimated >$20M spent. Craig reads that as a vote of no confidence by the other holder

  • Another set of really good assays, doing two things: infill to lift confidence (inferred to indicated) for the MRE due very soon, and gold outside known mineralised areas
  • BMT2 has no defined resource yet but keeps hitting gold: 28m @ 2, 25m @ ~1, 14m @ 1, 2m @ 5 g/t. It could become a new resource at the end of October
  • Expect a much bigger resource in the update in the next couple of weeks. The DFS is late-stage, due at year end

LPM (Lithium Plus Minerals) Bullish FA 00:15:07
  • Scoping study out today and the numbers look really good. Capex ~$87M, in line with Craig's expected $80-90M (preferably <$100M). Post-tax IRR ~75%, NPV ~$325M
  • DSO operation (dig, crush, sort, ship), so lower prices but no big processing capex. Close to infrastructure
  • Clear next steps and upside levers laid out. Targeting construction around Sep-Oct next year, with early offtake and finance discussions already underway (financing likely linked to offtake). Strong links to prominent lithium players
  • Caveats: DSO has no defined price (it's priced as a % of concentrate/hydroxide/carbonate), and lithium studies often show C1 costs with sustaining capex accounted for separately
  • Watch drilling into the main pegmatite and the adjacent pegmatite for a resource and mine-life upgrade over the next 3-6 months. Webinar tomorrow
  • Tip: read the product pricing/marketing section of scoping studies and PFSs for current market data. Here it used CXO's recent DSO fines sale as a live price comparison
QML (Queensland Mining / Qmines) Bullish FA 00:39:50
  • A member asked whether the constant stream of small drill-hole announcements hides something. So far all results are really good: they increase confidence in, and expand, the resource
  • Once assays are QA'd and complete, companies must release them; holding them would be withholding market information. Delays come from incomplete assays or waiting on an external competent person
  • Companies cherry-pick headlines (weaker holes sit in the tables), but QML's results are solid, consistent and sometimes better than before
  • Should make the resource upgrade and DFS better. Consistent with his prior Bullish call (6 Oct)

  • A member was frustrated by the cap raise into a 0.618 retrace after good results. Companies don't care about TA; they raise when the price and terms are attractive (or an investor offers a smaller discount)
  • Textbook exploration catalyst play from Fund 101: drilling an area analogous to known copper deposits (same trend), known high-grade hits, low market cap
  • Catalyst 1 (confirmation of high-grade copper): take a portion out. Catalyst 2 (extension at depth / a new lode): out completely, because the next ~30 holes would have to be extraordinary to extend the run

Session Themes

  • Capitulation psychology: it's designed to shake you out. Rely on your pre-set thesis, time frames and stops. Take stops when hit, act on a broken thesis, and stay busy preparing for the other side
  • Read the whole document: scoping-study marketing sections give current commodity pricing intelligence, and assay tables reveal what the headlines leave out. Check top cuts and grade smearing on high-grade intercepts
  • Don't conflate exploration (rock chips, channel samples) with a resource, or concepts (hub-and-spoke) with development
  • Catalyst plays need an exit plan: take wins as catalysts land (partial on catalyst 1, the rest on the continuation catalyst), and expect drift-back and cap raises after
  • Disclosure rules: QA'd assays must be released promptly, which explains steady streams of drill announcements
  • Watch out for retail pump-ups into trading halts (SPL) and thin-volume spikes in stalled stories (EM3)
  • Upcoming catalysts calendar: AUE MRE (end Oct), RCE DMC findings (mid-Nov), LPM drilling (3-6 months), EBR TGA approval (~May-June 2027). RXL question held over

Fundamental Analysis Scan with Craig Dickson

Bearish Setups: None

ODY (Odyssey Gold) Neutral FA 00:19:18
  • Craig's own position, found at a ~$35-40M market cap with ~400koz gold, existing mining leases and a growing resource. The plan was to toll-mill through the Kirkalocka restart, with a decision due by 30 September and production ~6 months later (Q1 2027)
  • JV partner Monument (20%, with a nearby ~300koz project and an old mill it's slow to refurbish) refused to sign an ore-sharing agreement. Right before the deadline, after 3 months of silence, it claimed ODY had breached JV conditions. "Monument is playing games"
  • The Kirkalocka processing deal and the near-term production timeline are gone, so Craig's thesis (decision in September, quick cash flow) is broken. He exited: "same as a stop loss being hit". No second-guessing, no bargaining, no moving the goalposts
  • Still positive on the company: a new deal sending ODY's 80% share of ore through Kirkalocka (leaving Monument's 20% in the ground) could be resolved within ~3 months, but mediation or court could drag on and there's no visibility on timing
  • Lookup note: his prior call was Bullish (29 Sep). Today's exit is a fresh thesis-break decision, not a bearish view of the business
SNM Bullish FA 00:24:28
  • Craig flagged it near its December lows. It ran, then fell "off a cliff" back to long-term support, but OBV did not follow the waterfall, so this is a huge area of interest
  • Fundamentals are much better than the first time: then ~1Moz (Columbia, historic/foreign resource, no drilling) at ~$35M market cap; now ~$28M market cap with ~2Moz across 2 projects
  • Bought Big Springs (Nevada, ~1Moz) from CMM. It already has an approved mine plan of operations and permits, about 10 years of work done. CMM also put ~$1M into the concurrent $15M raise at 58c
  • Next door to First Majestic's Jerritt Canyon restart, which needs mill feed, and management teams are mates. Big Springs is refractory, but there are ~4 roasters/autoclaves in the area that can process it
  • Columbia: difficult ground conditions and core loss, and the "Hail Mary" deep hole missed (that's fine). Drilling has confirmed historic results and extends gold outside the pit. JORC MRE conversion due mid-to-late November, a potential catalyst (could come in at or above ~1Moz)
  • Watch for the ~10,000m Big Springs drill program to kick off and more Columbia assays. A classic Craig setup: FA keeps improving while TA dumps into an area of interest without OBV support
  • Lookup: the prior FA entry was Bullish (29 Sep, pre-recorded) — today reaffirms with fresh analysis
EQU (Equus gas project) Bullish FA 00:32:07
  • ~$70-85M market cap holding one of Australia's largest known offshore gas resources (WA). ~$1-1.5B was spent on it historically by majors who couldn't make a standalone version work (~US$4B capex)
  • Picked up by a small private WA company in 2017. Their angle is a floating FPSO unit tied into existing WDS/STO pipelines and facilities, cutting billions off capex
  • Alcoa backing: a binding 10-year gas sales agreement (~50 TJ/day, ~25% of Alcoa's needs) plus ~US$30M funding pre-FEED and FEED up to FID
  • Pre-FEED for phase 1: NPV ~US$867M, revenue ~US$22B, ~52% EBITDA margin, payback 2 years after first gas, capex ~US$1.2B. Further phases are not yet included. WA LNG plants (Karratha, Pluto) face spare capacity by ~2030
  • Must bring in a strategic/operating partner, since small companies legally can't operate such assets. Candidates are Alcoa, WDS, STO or overseas players already in the data room. Partnering is targeted for 2027 (possibly H1)
  • Realistically first gas is ~2032. Timelines are the risk ("can you handle the timeline?"). The catalyst is the partnering deal closing. Smart money is positioning, and Craig hopes to have them on a call
AA2 Bullish FA 00:43:58
  • An under-the-radar Zimbabwe gold developer, Dokwe (Zimbabwe's largest undeveloped gold project): ~1.6Moz resource with a >1Moz reserve
  • PFS economics are among the best Craig has seen in gold: post-tax NPV ~A$1B, pre-tax IRR ~92% (post-tax high 70s), capex ~A$250M, very fast payback, 12-year life
  • Xinhai (major Chinese mining engineering, studies and build firm) took ~$8M at ~30c plus ~$1M and ~$2M share placements that fund met test work and the DFS. It also has an in-country Zimbabwe workforce
  • Management lives and breathes Zimbabwe, having taken two assets from exploration into production (dividends meant only ~2 cap raises in 10-15 years on the TSX). They've sold those stakes, leaving ~$50-60M cash vs an ~$81M market cap (more than half in cash)
  • Catalysts: more assays over ~3 months, met results, a bigger resource/reserve by year end (gold found outside the known resource), DFS in Q1 2027
  • Risks: dual-listed with low liquidity. Use the order book to nibble without paying the spread. "Ticks all the damn boxes". Consistent with his prior Bullish call (19 May)
FXG (Felix Gold) Neutral FA 00:51:10
  • A past FA winner (found before the antimony hype). It ran to a nice valuation without ever answering key questions and is now back at a very interesting level, ~$80-85M market cap
  • Still no antimony resource, no feasibility study, no mining permit lodged (the "100% permitted" claim is only bulk-sample/pilot permits) and no refinery site or study. The latest presentation was "so much fluff"
  • Positives: some of the world's highest-grade antimony hits (Treasure Creek), a simple direct-cast flow sheet (no concentrating or flotation, lower capex and ramp-up risk) proven at pilot scale, ~800koz inferred gold optionality, and a US critical-minerals funding tailwind
  • Mine permit expected around Q1 2027. Management says mining mid-next year; Craig expects September-October at the earliest
  • Craig thinks $80M is still pushing it and more downside wouldn't surprise him. Back on the radar TA- and FA-wise, but no rush. The big catalysts are an antimony MRE (grade and scale), then the feasibility study, then the Frontier refinery study
  • Lookup: the prior entry was Bullish (Sep 2025, during the run). Today is fresh analysis, and the shift to watching reflects that the valuation got ahead of fundamentals
FLG Bullish FA 00:32:38

NVA (Nova Minerals) Informational FA 00:51:41
  • Mentioned only as a comparison: like FXG once was, NVA has no studies on its antimony yet
CMM Informational FA 00:25:59

WDS / STO Informational FA 00:34:45
  • Mentioned as the owners of the pipelines and facilities EQU plans to tie into, and potential partners. Both are long aware of the project

Session Themes

  • Psychology in capitulation: it's normal and there's always another side. Lean on your community and mentors, zoom out to 1-4 year horizons, and use quiet periods to prepare
  • Thesis break = stop loss: exit when the thesis breaks even if you still like the company (ODY). Be more ruthless with TA stops and FA thesis breaks in markets where downside is amplified
  • Take profits earlier than usual; this market isn't giving long trends
  • Dividend-portfolio mindset (Lara's question): it means 5-10-30 year holding, accepting limited capital growth, needing millions in capital for full income, and not watching it like a day trade. FOMO wrecks dividend portfolios. Build capital first (or use SMSF capital) before a true income portfolio. Know yourself and don't adopt an identity that doesn't fit
  • FA + TA combo: improving fundamentals plus a price dump without OBV confirmation into a support area is a prime watch setup (SNM, FXG). Revisit past FA winners when charts return to old levels
  • Low-liquidity stocks: use the order book and buy in nibbles
  • Biotech catalysts (November into 2027) are still valid in any market. Craig's newspaper column is off this week for family reasons. FAQ Friday this week. A Gold Coast/Brisbane meet-up is coming

  • Defensive positioning in a jittery market: keep scanning and taking real buy signals, but use smaller parcels and very tight stops (the Darvas approach: if it doesn't go up, get out with a small loss). Accept that strings of small losses are good trading
  • Don't stay out forever either: a trader who sat out for 2 years after the 1987 crash, waiting for a second leg down, missed the whole rally
  • Buy-and-hold ETFs still need management. Trim when profits are being eaten away (QRE), and remember that time can work against you (PEN, DYL)
  • Overconfidence after a winning trade is dangerous. Be patient and wait for bottoming action and a resistance break before re-entering
  • Frank's trading tools are end-of-day data, OBV and saucers/ascending triangles; don't watch the market intraday

  • Key signal: financiers asked the company to re-run the study at current prices. Every time Craig has seen this near financing, a better report came out and financing closed within months. That makes the updated economics (better NPV/IRR) an "easy win" catalyst before FID

Session Themes

  • Resource-company stage cycles: exploration (early/mid/late), then development (early/mid/late), construction, ramp-up and production. Each stage has typical catalysts and typical chart behaviour. Play your stages, catalysts and value instead of riding the bull-market "passenger seat"
  • Signals near financing: financiers requesting re-run studies at current prices, a 10+ year mine life for large debt packages, and market cap large enough for lenders. Supportive specialist funds (Resource Capital Fund, Lion Selection) are a vote of confidence
  • Risk allocation like A/B/C-grade TA setups: size by how many odds are in your favour (geology, targeting, management, market cap/EV). Check market cap before every trade, including pure TA trades
  • Homework method: start with quarterlies and investor presentations, then specific announcements. Stage markers include soils/calcrete/rock chips (early exploration), foreign resource to JORC (mid exploration), scoping/PFS/EIA (development) and ramp-up (no AISC yet)
  • In a commodity super-cycle, pullbacks may be less savage, but cycles still zig and zag. FA entries give big early profits, which make free-carry and partial profit-taking easy
  • Liquidity: wide-spread micro caps are hard to use as short catalyst trades. Use the liquidity around the catalyst to exit, or treat them as 6-month to 2-year value holds
  • Next week: deposit size, drill widths, mapping and target generation, and how to read assay announcements

Macro Sunday

Hosted by Tung Nguyen | Sunday 18 October 2026
https://academy.masteringthemarkets.com/c/mtm-upcoming-events/macro-sunday-138fcf ↗
Bullish Setups: Gold, Silver, Gold & Silver Miners, Copper
Bearish Setups: US Dollar / US Debt & Treasuries
Neutral / Watching: Oil (Crude), Platinum / Palladium, Military Industrial Complex (Defence)
Gold Bullish Macro 00:03:06
  • Rick Rule's framing: if you're lucky you get three precious-metals bull markets in a lifetime (1970-80, 2000-11, and the current one that started ~2019). Tung and Dave are both "really, really bullish"
  • Rule saves in gold rather than USD/treasuries: he holds physical gold and sells some when he needs to buy something. Tung sees the same habit in multi-generational family offices
  • Rule's thesis: US debt passed $40tn this year and is growing ~$2tn/yr, with unfunded liabilities on top (~$126tn total, ~$378k per citizen). The only palatable way out is inflating it away, the 1970s playbook
  • Rule expects the USD to lose ~75% of its purchasing power over 10 years and is a buyer at 4400, 4600 and 4700. He warns that whatever drives gold higher is usually painful for the rest of your portfolio
  • 1970s analogue: gold went from $35 to $850 (~24x). The mid-cycle 1975-76 crash was 47% over ~18 months before new highs. The 2008 mid-cycle drop was ~38%. Tung held through this January's selloff because "we're only halfway through the cycle"
  • Inflation-adjusted, gold only broke above its 1980 high in December 2024, so the bull market can't be over yet. The Dow/Gold ratio hit a generational low in 2024 (as in 1929, 1966 and 1999), which marked a buy point
  • Central banks have been accumulating gold since ~2012 while selling US treasuries. Paper-vs-physical "musical chairs": there are ~152 paper claims per ounce of physical gold
  • Cycle timing: Tung expects the bull market to end around 2029-2030. Dave thinks it could run 1-2 years longer, a 12-13 year cycle in total
Silver Bullish Macro 00:22:18
  • This January silver crashed from ~$120 to ~$50, a mid-cycle correction Tung was expecting from the history. It is now ~$61, still ~20% above last year's conference level of $49
  • Rule treats silver as speculation (right side of the barbell) and gold as savings. He sold ~80% of his silver in August last year at ~$70-75 average (bought at ~$20s), rotated into more gold and into silver miners, and still thinks silver has more to go
  • Paper claims are ~404 per ounce of physical silver. In a run on physical, expect paper prices to fall while physical rises. Holding physical is an "option premium" on that event
  • Structural deficit for 6 years running (solar, EVs, data centres, electronics). Samsung partnered to reopen a Mexican silver mine to lock in supply, an example of a company securing its "chair"
  • Silver still hasn't broken above its inflation-adjusted 1980 high. Historically silver dramatically outperforms gold at the cycle top (1980, 2011), and Tung expects the same around 2029-30
  • Exit plan, gold/silver ratio (GSR): the GSR is ~67 now vs a ~61 long-term average. Past peaks bottomed at ~17 (1980) and ~35 (2011). Tung will start paying attention below 40 and sell in chunks at 40, 35 and 30, probably without waiting for 20
  • ~80% long-run correlation between oil and silver over 100 years of data
Gold & Silver Miners Bullish Macro 00:25:54
  • Rule: miners give better leverage. In the 1970s the average miner did ~50x vs gold's ~24x, and you don't need "penny dreadfuls" to get asymmetric returns
  • Rule suggests 50-75% of a precious-metals portfolio in the best large names (Newmont, Agnico Eagle, Wheaton, Franco-Nevada, Barrick) or an ETF, to "farm beta". Speculating in explorers only works if you back experienced management
  • 80/20 rule: most returns come from a small slice of juniors, and many juniors are "cockroaches" that go out of business
  • Tung, if starting today: he wouldn't buy hundreds of kilos of bullion now. He would allocate to silver and gold miners, the same move Rule made (Tung calls Rule "my seagull")
  • Rotation sequence: gold leads, silver confirms, then major miners, then juniors, moving further out the risk curve. Dave's miners-vs-metals ratio chart is only just breaking out after a long range, so this is "the very beginning"
  • Juniors vs majors hasn't broken out yet. A parabolic move in juniors would be the euphoria/excess-phase signal
  • Tung has cash on the sidelines and a couple of six-figure positions he wants to make. He prefers silver miners over defence because the silver deficit thesis isn't hostage to geopolitics
US Dollar / US Debt & Treasuries Bearish Macro 00:10:25
  • US public debt has passed $40tn and is growing ~$2tn a year. Unfunded liabilities (social security, Medicare, military and state pensions) take the total to ~$126tn
  • Three options: default on bonds, break promises to retirees (Tung doesn't think they'll do that), or inflate the debt away. Both Rule and Tung expect inflation
  • 1970s precedent: $1 bought 5 hamburgers in 1967 and 1 in 1982. Volcker needed 22% rates to break inflation and was the most hated man in the country
  • Hegemony is fading: US manufacturing peaked in the 1950s and China overtook ~2008-10. Japan, China and Russia have been selling treasuries (accelerating after Russian assets were confiscated) and rotating into gold
  • The US still holds military dominance, but its currency and debt standing is declining. The USD became the reserve currency after WWII partly because the US held ~80% of the world's gold
Copper Bullish Macro 00:57:19
  • Tung's favourite copper chart shows a structural deficit today, growing to a ~21 million tonne gap between demand and production by 2050
  • Precious-metals bull markets move alongside commodities and energy
  • Some manufacturing CEOs say they'd rather hold copper on the balance sheet than cash or US treasuries
Oil (Crude) Neutral Macro 00:57:19
  • Noted as up now, in line with its long-term ~80% correlation with silver
  • 1970s parallels: Yom Kippur War and the 1979 oil shock vs today's oil crisis. Used as macro context rather than a trade call
Platinum / Palladium Neutral Macro 00:59:53
  • Answering a chat question: Rule didn't cover palladium at the conference. In a podcast he called it more an industrial metal than a monetary one
  • Gold/silver investors are starting to diversify into platinum and palladium as a further hedge
Military Industrial Complex (Defence) Neutral Macro 01:00:54
  • Asked whether he's more bullish on defence than silver miners: Tung would pick silver miners
  • Defence is driven by capricious geopolitics (Ukraine or Gaza ending, a US president reconciling with NATO), any of which could break the thesis

Session Themes

  • "If you don't own any gold, you don't understand economics or history." Tung's family story: his father's release from a POW camp was paid for in gold after South Vietnam's currency collapsed (~90% devaluation, 1970-75)
  • History rhymes with the 1970s: inflation, an oil crisis, heavy money printing (25% of the USD money supply created in 18 months during COVID) and fading US hegemony
  • Barbell framework: gold on the safe side as savings and purchasing-power preservation, silver and miners on the speculative side for asymmetric returns
  • Expect sharp mid-cycle drawdowns: "if you can't handle the zigs, you don't deserve the zags." Eric Sprott held through an 85% drawdown in 2011-15 and is now a billionaire
  • Macro is early and a poor timing tool. Rule has no TA and still did well, while Dave, Jamie and Craig used TA to time their silver exits. There are many paths to financial independence
  • A show of hands moved from mixed views to ~90% agreeing the bull market is mid-cycle, which was the point of the talk: it's not too late

Session Themes

  • Opening mindset segment: a student's post shows 430 journaled trades, known win rates by market and day, and ~$80k in trading profit this year after spending his last ~$10k on the course. Journaling and data are what every successful trader has in common. Work on your skill and the money follows
  • Big-picture patience: Tung went from financially ruined (~2010) to fat FIRE in ~15 years, and his first million took 10 of those. Rick Rule had decades of ups and downs. Let time do the heavy lifting: the investment account is plan B, and trading profits fund it to get there faster
  • Concentration vs diversification: concentrate in ~5 high-conviction, well-researched asset classes to grow wealth, and diversify once you're protecting it. Either raise your education or reduce your exposure, so you can sleep at night holding big positions

  • Rotation toward defensives and hard assets (staples vs discretionary near a GFC-era breakout). Commodities may go through a bear-market "fluff around" before the big commodity leg
  • Q&A on the Tech 101 vs 201 course: 101 builds the foundations (expect about a year of applying them), the year-long course is for managing your super. Commitment and structure matter as much as content

Session Themes

  • Capital protection above all: exit on invalidation and re-enter later — small losses + one good trade beats holding through 30-90% drawdowns
  • Never hold trades through a weekly pivot; mark key levels and size holding decisions by the dollar amount you can afford to lose to the next level
  • Beginners stay on the daily timeframe; stay away from daily downtrends; don't get creative in a falling market
  • DCA only with a specific long-term thesis (he's only DCA-ing silver and BHP) — never on speculative uranium/lithium; better to layer in on the way up
  • Shorting for income targets B-wave bounces and S/R flips, not tops
  • Financials (CBA preferred, ANZ, NAB, XFJ) are his current long focus; tech remains a no
  • Hidden bullish divergence = continuation strength (Term 2 content); pivots are the foundation for seeing it
  • Return expectations: think annually (~30%/yr achievable with skill), not a fixed monthly %

Session Themes

  • Yields are the key macro driver: the US 10-year is in its final wave 5 (target 5.4-5.8%), and its top should mark a bond bottom and a rotation out of risk assets (stocks, crypto) into bonds — historically followed by 20-57% S&P drawdowns
  • Narrow market: mega caps (Mag 7) are carrying the S&P while equal-weight, small caps and KOSPI-led tech weaken — breadth warning
  • ASX sector rotation playing out as called: rate holds are lifting financials, discretionary, staples and utilities; healthcare is near a wave 1 top (buy the Jan-Feb pullback); telcos and tech remain weak
  • Risk-off sentiment: uranium, lithium, rare earths and small-cap metals are at "areas of interest", but that's not a buy — wait for buyers to step in. Craig is holding significant cash for the flush-out
  • Precious metals: gold/platinum strong and measured; silver/palladium deep; key gold level ~4,140. Use GDX/gold, AG/silver and MSTR/BTC divergences to identify classic tops and bottoms
  • Trading news events (CPI): expect a liquidity sweep of both highs and lows; the safe trade is to fade the initial move once it pivots. CPI methodology change (~0.3-0.4% lower) may cause a knee-jerk bullish surge
  • Lower-timeframe trading: focus on the Asia, London and New York opens — AMD (accumulation, manipulation, distribution); London sweeping Asia's high/low sets the directional bias for New York. Favourite indicators: FVG and Market Sessions by ange1991
  • Elliott Wave tools: wave 5 targets via 0.618 or 1.272-1.618 extensions; C waves out of triangles project the triangle height; the 0.786 is his preferred wave 2 level; invalidated counts mean wait, not catch falling knives

  • Market is still range-bound near the lows of a long sideways range; OBV hints at accumulation but direction is unclear. In a weak market he uses the same buy signals, just gets fewer of them and takes smaller positions

  • Dividend-gap ETF trades (AGX1, GLOB): buy after the distribution gap and wait for the gap to close, collecting high yield — "hold indefinitely until something better comes along"
  • Position management: stopped out of COH and TAH (time stop/boredom); "boredom is a killer"; capital size matters — bigger accounts can take every signal, smaller ones must concentrate (one focused position can be watched better)
  • Cap raises: check cash runway in the latest reports before buying small caps; ignore the halt period
  • Breakout rules: 3+ months of resistance before buying the break, stop a tick below the latest prominent low, saucer depth projected for targets, OBV should follow the saucer shape; Fibonacci retracements alone aren't buy signals
  • Long-term "buy and hold" blue chips like WDS, STO, TLS have gone nowhere for 10-20 years — question whether there's a better stock
  • Doesn't trade crypto — only instruments on a recognised stock exchange

Macro Sunday

Hosted by Tung Nguyen | Sunday 11 October 2026
https://academy.masteringthemarkets.com/c/mtm-upcoming-events/macro-sunday-be1b44 ↗
Bullish Setups: RBA Cash Rate / AU Interest Rates (rates rising), Gold, Cash / Money Market Funds, Gold, Silver & Copper Miners, Emerging Markets / Rest of World vs US, Bitcoin / Crypto
Bearish Setups: Australian Residential Property, Australian Economy (unemployment / inflation / fiscal position), US Treasuries / Sovereign Bonds, S&P 500 / Nasdaq, US Tech / AI (data centre capex), US Consumer (credit / delinquencies), US Residential Property, US Commercial Real Estate
Neutral / Watching: Oil (Crude)
Australian Residential Property Bearish Macro 00:05:06
  • Friends trying to sell for months are "chasing a market in perennial decline" — like getting rid of a falling knife; some markets have headline prices down 20% and still can't sell
  • Perth and Darwin remain the more resilient markets
  • Don't be over-leveraged — the last thing you want to be is a forced seller; a coaching client who added property and debt last year is now stuck as rates rise
  • 18-year property cycle points to a bottom somewhere between 2027 and 2030 — "a couple more years to go"
  • Tung is not planning to buy back into property: CGT and negative gearing changes are a secular shift that dissuades investors (homeowners still need a home), so prices normalise
  • Pockets of value will still appear — a friend bought a distressed cash sale for $5m that the bank then valued at $7.5m
Australian Economy (unemployment / inflation / fiscal position) Bearish Macro 00:11:56
  • Unemployment is trending up, currently 4.6% and rising — not far off the ~6% GFC peak (the early-90s recession peaked around 11%)
  • Believes the real unemployment / underemployment rate is far higher, masked by people pivoting to part-time and gig work
  • Founder of Finder announced he is leaving Australia for Singapore; Tung's Savvy post drew 700 comments in a day, mostly "good riddance" — a read on the "S" in PESTLE (sentiment running hot because people are hurting)
  • Macro reality: government spending exceeds tax receipts; each multimillionaire who leaves shrinks receipts, so the gap is filled by higher taxes on those who remain and/or more borrowing
  • Australia's debt-to-GDP is still relatively healthy (40s) versus the US (120s) and Japan (250s)
  • Only two levers protect you whatever happens: asset allocation and position size
RBA Cash Rate / AU Interest Rates Bullish Macro 00:14:16
  • October inflation print rose to 5.3%, now above the RBA cash rate — "they're going to have to increase rates"
  • RBA has to get ahead of CPI and push it back below its 3% target — a big gap from 5.3%
  • Believes real inflation is well above the official number (school fees, insurance, pickleball court hire doubling from $5 to $10)
  • Expect more rate rises and more mortgage increases ahead
  • Bias tag refers to the direction of rates (higher), which is a headwind for property and households
US Treasuries / Sovereign Bonds Bearish Macro 00:23:24
  • Not a fan of the classic 60/40 portfolio — bonds no longer hedge equities; we are in a secular bear market for bonds
  • Bonds have fallen about 67% peak-to-trough since March 2020; best time to own bonds is when yields are ~15% and falling, not now
  • Rising rates destroy the value of existing lower-coupon bonds — advisers recommending bonds for diversification are using an old playbook
  • World is at the "front doorstep of a sovereign debt crisis" (the GFC was a private-sector debt crisis)
  • Ray Dalio clip: US debt above $40 trillion, spending ~$7tn vs ~$5tn revenue (40% more than it takes in), 30-year yields heading toward 6%
  • Central banks are pivoting away from holding US Treasuries; USD and Treasuries no longer work on the "safe" left side of the barbell
  • Revisited at 01:06:18: US rates at an 18-year high since the Iran war; borrowing costs up in one year — Japan 30-year +36%, France 10-year +40%, US +19% — "completely unheard of"
Gold Bullish Macro 00:31:58
  • The remaining left-side-of-the-barbell asset now that USD (inflation) and Treasuries (rising rates) are being eroded
  • Central banks keep buying gold — their long time horizon means volatility doesn't dissuade them
  • Downside is volatility: gold recently had a 3% one-day sell-off; research shows only 57 of 5,378 sessions (~1%) had a >3% one-day drop
  • That volatility is what keeps retail and some institutions away, but on a long enough horizon it doesn't worry him
Cash / Money Market Funds Bullish Macro 00:35:51
  • Record ~$8 trillion sitting in US money market funds — deep pockets can't see value with the S&P at all-time highs and AI expensive
  • Sitting on the sidelines with cash is "probably the smart thing to do" — Munger: sometimes the hardest and smartest thing is to do nothing
  • Berkshire did the same into the GFC and then bought aggressively after the crash
  • If you don't know what to buy, holding cash for a while is fine; being cashed up when bargains appear is the best position to be in
  • Tung says he has never held so much cash in his life
S&P 500 / Nasdaq Bearish Macro 00:38:52
  • S&P at all-time highs but "egregiously expensive" with very narrow breadth: only ~44% of S&P stocks are above their 200-day moving average
  • 82% of US stocks are 10%+ below their highs, 59% are 20%+ below, 41% are 30%+ below — a handful of ~10 tech names is carrying the index
  • US is ~45% of global equity exposure (China/HK 16%, Europe 13%, rest of APAC 11%, Japan 6%) — a "stool with one leg"
  • Tung has no US exposure and no broad equity exposure other than miners; told his son to avoid a global growth fund with 60-70% US allocation
  • His son holds only Nasdaq (long-run technology wins), ASX 200 (resources-heavy) and a Bitcoin ETF — new DCA money is going to the ASX and Bitcoin, not the US
  • Global equity fund flows have shown a couple of weeks of outflows — not conclusive; would want ~6 consecutive worsening weeks before calling "get out of dodge"
  • Grantham clip: "don't own US stocks"; the days of simply dollar-cost-averaging a global growth index are over for the next decade — you will need real skills (macro sectors or fundamentals)
  • Timing: thinks it hits the fan "probably sometime next year" — the Wile E. Coyote moment
Gold, Silver & Copper Miners Bullish Macro 00:41:11
  • The only equity exposure Tung currently holds: gold mining, silver mining and copper mining
  • Now is the time to be very selective about sectors rather than own broad indices
  • ASX 200 favoured for his son's DCA because it is resources-heavy
US Tech / AI (data centre capex) Bearish Macro 00:44:12
  • Tech sector to S&P ratio at 0.56 (recent high ~0.6) — the last time tech was this over-represented was the March 2000 dot-com peak
  • AI, data centres and tech will keep changing the world, but they are overvalued relative to the rest of the market — "obviously a bubble"
  • Dalio: the single biggest risk is concentration in one exciting asset like AI
  • All other private construction capex has been in free fall since 2024 while data centre capex soars — unsustainable because of the divergence and because it is funded by savings/borrowings that are getting more expensive as rates rise
  • Grantham: AI is arguably the biggest investment bubble ever; would sell big US tech positions
  • After 2000 even Microsoft took ~15 years to regain its peak — Tung is sitting out US and tech stocks
  • He "loves bubbles" — the macro investor's job is to catch them early, exit, and rotate to the next wave
Emerging Markets / Rest of World vs US Bullish Macro 00:54:08

  • Grantham favours emerging markets and mentions Australia
  • Better to allocate capital to markets other than the US at the moment
Bitcoin / Crypto Bullish Macro 00:57:08
  • Disagrees with Grantham's "Bitcoin goes to zero" — doesn't think Bitcoin has had its bubble yet
  • Litmus test for mainstream adoption: banks like CBA stop fighting it, it is as easy to buy through CBA as an exchange, and industry super funds offer exposure — not there yet
  • Described as "relatively cheap" at the moment (00:44:12); his son holds a Bitcoin ETF and is adding via DCA
US Consumer (credit / delinquencies) Bearish Macro 00:58:39
  • US revolving consumer credit at all-time highs — the highest-interest, worst type of debt, and it is rising because people can't pay it down
  • Serious credit card delinquencies about 10% for 18-29 year olds and 8.3% for 30-39 year olds
  • Consumer confidence at 81.9 — not GFC lows (~25) but worse than during COVID
  • Consumers are the weakest balance sheet in the chain (households < companies < banks < countries)
US Residential Property Bearish Macro 01:02:29
  • Banks are seizing 42% more homes as Americans fall behind on mortgages — significant because the home is the last debt people stop paying
  • US real estate ETF relative to the S&P peaked in 2007 and has been in secular decline since
  • May bottom around 2027-2030 on the 18-year property cycle, after which property could look attractive again relative to the S&P
US Commercial Real Estate Bearish Macro 01:03:15
  • Commercial mortgage-backed securities delinquency rate is now worse than during the GFC
  • Driven by the post-COVID secular shift to hybrid work — companies have realised they don't need as much office space
Oil (Crude) Neutral Macro 01:06:18
  • Shares a clip arguing Iran now effectively controls US interest rates: if the Fed hikes whenever oil spikes, whoever controls oil prices controls the Fed
  • Tanker and refinery attacks around the Strait of Hormuz / Bab al-Mandeb clustered before the Fed's July and 16 September meetings, pushing oil back above $100 a barrel
  • Brent rose more than 60% in March after the strait was declared closed
  • Date to watch: next Fed decision on 28 October
  • Tung "can't fault the logic" — no directional trade given; the point is oil-driven inflation keeping rates higher

Session Themes

  • A little bit of macro goes a long way — you can see trouble months ahead and get your ducks in order instead of becoming a forced seller
  • Strip feelings out: the economics doesn't care; the only two levers are asset allocation and position size
  • The winners of the last decade (tech, S&P, property) probably won't be what makes you rich in the next decade — diversification is the topic of the upcoming MtM Live in Melbourne
  • Sovereign debt crisis risk is building across the US, Japan and Europe as borrowing costs jump
  • Concentration risk: an overvalued sector, in an over-represented country, with most stocks below their 200-day average
  • Patience and no FOMO — hold cash, wait for clarity, and buy undervalued assets when bargains emerge
  • Value investing and stock/sector-picking skills will matter again; passive global-index DCA will be much harder for the next decade
