FA in Practice - Meet MD and CEO of ALK (Alkane Resources)

Hosted by Craig Dickson | Monday 07 September 2026
Bullish Setups: ALK
Bearish Setups: None
Neutral / Watching: None
ALK (Alkane Resources) Bullish FA 00:00
  • Guest interview with Nick Earner, CEO of Alkane Resources, who has led the company for nearly a decade (started as COO for Tomingley and the former Dubbo rare earths project before being promoted).
  • Three producing mines after the ~1-year-old merger with TSX-listed Mandalay Resources: Tomingley (NSW gold, ~83koz last year), Costerfield (VIC, gold + antimony, ~45koz gold-equiv last year, still the largest Western antimony producer at ~2,000t this year), and Björkdal (Sweden gold, ~41-43koz last year, targeting 50-55koz). Combined guidance ~170koz this year vs 168koz last year.
  • Merger rationale: solved Alkane's liquidity/growth-perception problem (market wasn't rewarding a single low-growth asset) and Mandalay's liquidity problem (4 shareholders had owned 80%+ of the register); Earner described it as low-drama and well-timed against rising gold price tailwinds.
  • Financial position: ~$2.5bn AUD market cap, $400m+ available liquidity, ~15% of ASX trading volume replicated nightly on the TSX. Declared its first-ever dividend (2c fully franked) alongside a parallel buyback (aimed at North American holders who don't benefit from franking credits) — kept deliberately conservative to be sustainable/growing rather than maximised immediately.
  • Cost discipline: guidance is for all-in sustaining costs just under $3,000 AUD/oz; Earner said he personally prefers the stricter "all-in cost" measure (including growth capital), which comes out closer to ~$4,200 AUD/oz on a mature, steady-state basis — and flagged that as a sensible level for investors/lenders to stress-test the business at, well below the current ~$6,000 AUD gold price.
  • Boda-Kaiser (flagship growth project): 15Moz gold-equivalent resource (~10Moz indicated), grading ~0.3g/t gold + ~0.2% copper (~0.58g/t AuEq). Discovery hole was 2019 (~$40m+ spent drilling to indicated status by 2024). The 2024 scoping study was done at much lower gold/copper prices than today, so current economics are described as far more robust. Pre-feasibility study due back-half of 2027, running in parallel with environmental/land approvals; targeting production in the "early 2030s" at an initial ~220koz/year, which could help move Alkane toward a 400koz+ producer profile. Capital scale flagged as likely $2bn+.
  • Peak Hill (near-term optionality): ~110koz existing resource near Tomingley, a refractory ore body requiring oxidative treatment (pressure oxidation/BIOX/atmospheric leach); ongoing infill/step-out drilling with assay results expected in the next month or two. Earner said it's economically "very, very feasible" to process via a relatively small (illustratively ~$50m) circuit feeding into Tomingley's existing CIL plant, particularly at current gold prices.
  • M&A/capital allocation stance: no longer taking small stakes in ASX juniors (recently sold its Sky Metals position, holds a diluted ~4% in MMA) since junior explorers again have ready access to equity/debt markets; now prefers full-control transactions. Described the "ideal" acquisition target as a single-asset producer whose growth is capital-constrained (i.e. Alkane's own former profile), and said the company would also consider early-production names in operational distress if the root cause is fixable (plant/operating issues) rather than geological (which caps genuine upside).
  • Jurisdiction commentary: flagged interest in further Scandinavian gold assets (western Finland/northern Sweden belt) to sit alongside Björkdal, but noted opportunities have been shrinking as majors (e.g. Agnico) also compete for undeveloped ground given the higher gold price.
  • Craig's framing throughout was strongly positive, repeatedly praising Alkane's predictability/consistency ("boring" as a compliment), free-cash-flow discipline, and multi-year forward planning (land acquisition, permitting, exploration) as the standout traits versus peers who overpromise on growth ("aspirational 2030 plan" style slides).
  • Earner's own investing framework, offered to viewers: judge producers on underlying free cash flow generation (not accounting profit), mine-life/reserve replacement visibility (5-year line of sight, growth options out to 10 years), and demonstrated reliability in meeting guidance; reserve "5-10 bagger" return expectations for higher-risk exploration/development names, not established multi-asset producers like Alkane.

Session Themes

  • Deep dive into how a mid-cap multi-asset gold producer actually runs long-range planning: annual (July-June) budget cycles, layering gold-price and production assumptions onto internal life-of-mine plans, and maintaining a minimum liquidity buffer plus an untapped revolving credit facility "for when you don't need it."
  • Extensive discussion of the New South Wales project-approval process for moving a highway to unlock the Roswell/San Antonio open cuts at Tomingley (flora/fauna studies, biodiversity offsets, agricultural land impact, water studies, land acquisition from farmers) — used as a real-world illustration of how long and capital-intensive (a ~$30m "risk decision" on exploration drives alone) de-risking a growth project actually is before construction.
  • Antimony market context: explained why gold still dominates revenue (~97% of Costerfield's revenue vs. ~3% from antimony despite Alkane being the largest Western antimony producer) and why the antimony price is small, illiquid and heavily influenced by Chinese export policy and solar-panel/glass demand rather than the "military demand" narrative commonly cited.
  • Recurring theme: distinguishing genuine free-cash-flow-backed valuation from speculative growth narratives — Earner was critical of the recent ASX trend of companies publishing long-dated "aspirational" production targets without a funded basis, contrasting that with Alkane's preference to only communicate what current projects can actually support.
  • Explained the trade-offs of different ways to monetise Boda-Kaiser (outright sale, minority sell-down with offtake, majority sell-down for a free-carry) and why that decision is realistically a "2029 question" once permitting and pre-feasibility work is further advanced.

Macro Sunday (Pre-Recorded)

Hosted by Tung Nguyen | Sunday 06 September 2026
Bullish Setups: Perth / WA Property, Darwin / Northern Territory Property, Commercial Property, New Zealand Property / Airbnb Arbitrage
Bearish Setups: Australian Residential Property (national), Australian Bank Stocks
Neutral / Watching: None
Australian Residential Property (National) Bearish Macro 00:07:30
  • Fresh CBA analysis cited: national peak-to-trough decline of ~9-10%, with Sydney (~13%) and Melbourne (~12%) hit hardest; Tung treats this as a reasonable base case that could still be worse.
  • The downturn is broad and correlated — falling prices reported across ~90% of Australian suburbs, which Tung reads as clear evidence macro/liquidity forces (not individual property quality) are the dominant driver right now.
  • Demand-side drivers all turned negative in the last 12-18 months: banks tightening lending standards, real wages back to ~2011 levels after inflation, and the recent removal of negative gearing on new purchases plus a new 30% minimum capital gains tax on investment property.
  • Supply side is also weak but for different reasons — construction industry insolvencies remain elevated (~3,000/yr now vs ~1,000 in 2021), which constrains new supply and may cushion (but not prevent) the price falls.
  • Using his 18-year property cycle framework, Tung places 2026 near the cycle peak, with a trough expected around 2027-2030 — comparable in depth to the 2017 and 2022 corrections (~12-13%), not as severe as 2008 (~6%, cushioned then by the China commodities boom).
  • Personal/practical takeaway shared for his son: prioritise buying a first home but be wary of over-leveraging into a falling market; using the First Home Super Saver Scheme (effectively a risk-free ~15% return via the tax saving) to build a deposit for a possible entry point around 2030.
Perth / WA Property Bullish Macro 00:10:30
  • Standout exception to the broader downturn — Perth and WA behave like "a different country" economically due to ~40% dependence on mining/resources.
  • Tied directly to Tung's ongoing commodities-supercycle thesis; he expects the WA property tailwind to persist for roughly another decade, drawing a parallel to the 2008-2014 cycle where Perth kept rising through the GFC before topping out with the commodities cycle around 2014-15.
  • WA construction insolvencies down ~17% year-on-year — read as a genuine demand-strength signal, not just a smaller market producing smaller numbers.
Darwin / Northern Territory Property Bullish Macro 00:10:00
  • The one region bucking the national correction entirely — Darwin prices reportedly hit new highs as of the July data while every other capital city declined.
  • Northern Territory insolvencies also down (vs. rising elsewhere), reinforcing the read that underlying demand there is genuinely stronger, not just calmer.
  • Named alongside Perth as the two markets Tung would choose if forced to deploy new property capital today.
Australian Bank Stocks Bearish Macro 00:59:00
  • ~70% of Australian lending is property/housing-related, so a multi-year property downturn plus rising construction-sector insolvencies flow through as credit risk to the major banks.
  • Tung explicitly said he wouldn't be allocating new capital into bank stocks right now given this exposure.
Commercial Property & New Zealand Property / Airbnb Arbitrage Bullish Macro 00:59:00
  • Capital rotation theme: as negative gearing and residential tax incentives are removed, Tung sees money pivoting into alternatives.
  • Commercial property: better yields (tenants typically cover outgoings), lower landlord maintenance burden, though higher borrowing costs and complexity — cited a friend who built substantial wealth this way and only re-entered the market this year after being out for ~4-5 years, which Tung reads as a positive demand signal from a "smart investor."
  • New Zealand property: no capital gains tax there, drawing Australian investor interest (with the caveat that the ATO will still pursue its share on eventual repatriation/citizenship interactions).
  • Airbnb arbitrage highlighted as the model Tung is actively pushing to his own son as the new playbook for younger investors: rent (not buy) properties, furnish and sublet via Airbnb, ideally with an outsourced virtual team handling operations — pitched as needing far less upfront capital than a traditional 20% deposit while potentially generating stronger net cash flow than negatively-geared residential property.

Session Themes

  • Full-session deep dive built around Tung's demand/supply macro framework for property: demand side = population growth, immigration, credit availability, employment, real wage growth, tax incentives; supply side = land availability, zoning, infrastructure, construction costs/capacity — with commentary on which specific drivers have shifted (turned negative) in the past 12-18 months.
  • Core message: the traditional Australian "buy-and-negatively-gear residential property" wealth model has structurally shifted following the negative gearing removal and 30% minimum CGT change, requiring investors to consider alternatives (WA/NT property, commercial property, NZ property, Airbnb arbitrage) rather than assume the old playbook still works.
  • Recurring philosophy: macro tells you where capital is likely to rotate and the broad direction (the "tide"), while technical analysis (Dave/Craig/Jamie's frameworks) supplies the timing — the two are complementary, not substitutes.
  • Personal/lifestyle segment on returning from a 2-month "geo-arbitrage" trip through Japan and Malaysia, an upcoming November "designing your FIRE lifestyle" masterclass focused on diversification, and further overseas travel plans (Vietnam, a FIRE conference, Philippines) later in the year.
  • Tung was explicit that his own tax/structuring commentary (e.g. buying an investment property he intends to eventually move into to manage future CGT) is personal opinion, not financial or tax advice.

FA in Practice - Meet both the CEO and the MD of Adavale Resources (ADD)

ADD (Adavale Resources) Bullish FA 00:00
  • Guest interview with Alan (Chairman/CEO, ex-investment banker with decades in resources at HP, Rio, Exxon, BP) and David (MD, geologist, ~12 months in the role) of Adavale Resources.
  • Flagship asset: London Victoria gold project near Parkes, NSW (Lachlan Fold Belt / Parkes Thrust) — a historic open pit mined by BHP in the late 1980s-90s (~155,000oz at 1.5g/t) that closed only because gold fell below US$400/oz; never reopened for gold since.
  • Current resource is 115,000oz (inferred), based purely on old BHP drilling — does NOT yet include ADD's own recently completed 85-hole drill program.   • Major de-risking factor: the site already has a working BHP-built processing plant (currently used commercially by a limestone quarry operator) and an existing tailings dam, plus development approvals already in place for drill/blast/process on site — refurbishment estimated ~$10m (quoted 13 years ago) vs building new (cited recent comparable capex of $150-300m for a from-scratch plant).
  • Favourable strip ratio — ore body sits close to surface/pit floor, so minimal waste stripping needed to reach ore (~100m of open pit development cited).
  • Standout assay results discussed: 19m at 4g/t (incl. a high-grade interval reported as 0.5m at 15g/t / 31.1g/t troy), and a historic zone re-assayed 8 times in 1996 averaging 245g/t (range ~190-280g/t) at only ~25m depth — repeatability cited as confirming grade is real, not a one-off.
  • Land package: 610 sq km across 8 tenements spanning a 70km strike of the Parkes Thrust; ADD now holds the dominant southern half (neighbour Alkane, a ~$3bn company, holds the north). Package built via staged deals over ~12-18 months, including licenses acquired from Alkane and the recent Orange Minerals (OMX) acquisition.
  • Other targets in the portfolio: Victoria South (same deposit extension, already drilled at tight spacing, enough holes to be included in the imminent resource update at inferred level), Caleri (20km south, past underground workings, potential satellite feed for a London Victoria plant), and Ashes (porphyry copper-gold IP target near North Parkes, drilling targeted before end of 2026).
  • Corporate: ~400m shares on issue, share price ~4c, market cap ~$16m, cash ~$2m (per last quarterly, prior to recent drilling spend). Directors take shares instead of cash salary (~6.4% combined holding); a well-known cornerstone investor (unnamed, described as an early Paladin and large Oceana shareholder) holds ~21%.
  • Craig Dickson's framing was strongly bullish throughout — repeatedly praised the deliberate, low-profile land consolidation strategy and directors' skin-in-the-game (no cash salaries), and compared ADD's trajectory to Waratah Minerals (WTM), which the same vendor backed from ~$3m to $250m+ market cap in under 3 years, calling ADD a potential "baby Waratah."
  • Plan/sequence: resource upgrade (imminent) → scoping study → near-term production at London Victoria, with regional exploration (Ashes, Victoria South, Caleri) run in parallel without distracting from the core production path.

Session Themes

  • FA in Practice format: direct company management interview rather than chart-based analysis.
  • Craig's checklist for judging a small-cap resource story: management skin-in-the-game (shares vs cash salary), quality/track record of cornerstone shareholders, staged/deliberate land consolidation vs scattergun approach, existing infrastructure and approvals as capex/time de-risking factors, and balancing near-mine resource growth against speculative "hail mary" exploration.
  • Repeated emphasis on primary evidence over promotion: historic BHP drilling, repeat assay verification, and existing development approvals cited as concrete de-risking factors rather than management talking points.

Session Themes

  • Central message: a sharp portfolio drawdown does not automatically invalidate a trading thesis — markets alternate between expansionary "zig" and corrective "zag" phases, and traders need to assess whether structure has actually changed rather than reacting to discomfort.
  • Gaps are most useful read alongside momentum and structure — repeated downside gaps into oversold conditions can mark capitulation rather than an invitation to sell (and vice versa for overbought upside gaps).
  • Volume distinguishes continuation from failure: declining volume on a retracement can signal reduced selling pressure, while persistent selling through an expected support (e.g. Sonic Healthcare) confirms a thesis is failing.
  • Recurring setup pattern: an initial impulsive move, a deep second-wave retracement, former sellers becoming buyers in the "zag" zone, then a higher low and break of the declining structure before entry.
  • Monthly timeframe context matters — a sharp early-month decline can look severe on the daily chart but end up as just a lower wick on the monthly candle.
  • Portfolio management doesn't require every trade to work — a small number of major trends (CSL, Woodside, Santos, Woolworths) drive most of the growth, while small wins/losses roughly offset elsewhere; favourable reward-to-risk (e.g. risk 1% for ~3%) reduces reliance on a high win rate.
  • Psychological note: knowing a correction is likely doesn't remove the emotional impact of a fast, broad decline — discomfort is not evidence; only price, volume or structure invalidating the plan should trigger an exit.

LTR (Liontown Resources) Bullish FA 00:52:21

Session Themes

  • Give post-earnings price action time (1-2 weeks) to settle before trusting the technical structure — big moves right after results are often institutions repricing/repositioning rather than an organic trend, and a clearer technical + fundamental picture emerges once that imbalance clears.
  • Distinguish a real earnings-driven "waterfall/rocket" move from a normal orderly trend — the destination can still matter, but the route doesn't confirm a healthy setup.
  • Revenue growth must be weighed against cost growth (GDG) — top-line growth without margin/cash-flow improvement is lower quality.
  • Capital preservation as the central discipline: avoiding uncertain earnings events, financially distressed operators (TER) and promotional early-stage stories (VKA) may mean missing occasional rallies, but protects against risks of permanent capital loss.
  • Metallurgical/resource-definition derisking (PVT, QML, KZR, BTM) treated as high-value, lower-drama catalysts that strengthen existing projects even without new-discovery headlines.
  • September ex-dividend dates can produce price drops that reflect the dividend payment, not necessarily business deterioration — don't misread these as bearish signals.

Craig sees this as a strong smart-money signal and plans to ask them directly about it at the upcoming Gold Coast mining conference.

Session Themes

  • Reading beyond headline scoping-study numbers: CST showed how "real" CAPEX (including pre-production OPEX and sustaining/refining capex) can be materially higher than the top-line figure the market first reacts to.
  • Valuation discipline on high-PE growth stories (DUG) — the bigger the PE multiple, the bigger the growth expectations baked in, and the bigger the downside risk if growth disappoints.
  • Two major, well-received capital raises on the same day (BKB and BHM) — both framed as funding accelerated drilling/development rather than shoring up a weak balance sheet, which Craig treats as a bullish signal.
  • Corporate/insider positioning as a research signal — Forrestania's stake-building in CAV echoed as a reason for extra conviction.
  • Strategic-fit scrutiny on M&A — Liontown's move into an unrelated brine project drew caution despite being a logical partnership on paper.

BVR (Pickle Crow) Neutral FA + TA 01:14:55

  • Technically lacks the clean impulse structure preferred for high-probability setups — declining volume, no convincing bullish anchor.
  • A potential triangle within the downtrend is a caution flag (Elliott triangles typically sit in wave 4s/B-waves and can precede another leg down), plus hidden bearish momentum characteristics.
  • Preferred approach: monitor only, don't anticipate a breakout.
CBA (Commonwealth Bank) Neutral FA + TA 01:23:51
  • Headline numbers (statutory profit, cash profit, EPS, dividend) looked strong, but forward indicators are weakening: softer FY26 home-loan applications, rising impairment expense, higher arrears, and more troublesome/non-performing exposures.
  • Management's own outlook flagged slower growth, weaker household demand, higher rates, renewed inflation pressure and softer housing activity into FY27 — the earnings sell-off was framed as fundamentally justified, not overdone.
  • Technically sitting in a well-defined triangle within the larger advance; preferred Elliott count leaves room for one final fifth-wave push (potentially ~30% from the lower region) after a prior wave three that hit a high-probability 1.618 extension.
  • Framed explicitly as a possible late-cycle move, not a new long-term trend — the triangle is the key invalidation: a breakdown would materially weaken the fifth-wave case and shouldn't be dismissed just because CBA "always recovers."

Session Themes

  • Central framing: the best opportunities show up when fundamentals, catalysts and technical structure independently point the same way (PDN and NIC were the clearest examples) — neither discipline needs to "prove" the other.
  • Repeated distinction between an attractive company/story and an attractive entry — MMA and BML are quality names where a lot of success is already priced in, while SEEK shows the reverse (shaky fundamentals, still a plausible technical trade).
  • Mine development stage was used as a risk lens: exploration vs. construction vs. ramp-up vs. steady-state production all carry very different risk profiles (PDN de-risking, BML in higher-risk construction, MMA using Cosmic Boy to soften its own ramp-up risk).
  • Strip ratios flagged as a useful, often-overlooked cost driver for miners — higher waste-to-ore ratios raise unit costs, lower ratios help margins.
  • CBA used as the case study for why headline earnings aren't enough — forward indicators (applications, arrears, impairments, management outlook) are often priced in before they show up in the headline numbers.
  • Strong push for simple, repeatable setups over complexity: a technically valid trade doesn't have to be taken just because it can be explained — patience and comfort with inactivity were repeated psychological themes, alongside not letting a compelling macro story (e.g. uranium) override stops on an individual position.

Macro Sunday

Hosted by Tung Nguyen | Sunday 30 August 2026
Bullish Setups: Commodities / Western Australia property
Bearish Setups: None
Neutral / Watching: S&P 500, Australian Housing / Property (NSW, Victoria)
S&P 500 Neutral Macro 00:20:47
  • Index remains near record/historically elevated levels even as parts of the consumer economy weaken — Tung flagged this as an important macro divergence, not a timing signal.
  • Roughly 92% of the economy estimated to be growing at under 1%, versus ~8% growing at ~13% — a "K-shaped" split Tung sees as masked by strong headline index levels.
  • Retailers like JB Hi-Fi and Walmart cited as better real-time reads on underlying consumer stress than the index itself.
  • Comparison drawn to conditions preceding the dot-com and GFC periods — strong markets alongside weakening household finances.
  • Not a bearish call on the index itself; framed as a reason to stay disciplined rather than assume passive broad exposure keeps working the way it has historically.
Australian Housing / Property Neutral Macro 00:25:18
  • Melbourne house prices have gone from roughly 3x annual income historically to 8-10x today; NSW is around 12x income — used as the clearest evidence of structural affordability deterioration.
  • New South Wales: elevated price-to-income multiple flagged as the most exposed to a meaningful correction (revisited ~00:28:06).
  • Victoria: comparatively weaker conditions following policy changes affecting investor, foreign, and short-term accommodation buyers (~00:27:57).
  • Western Australia: relatively more valuation headroom, benefiting from a lower starting base and the commodities cycle — the one bright spot in the property discussion.
  • Overall framing: treat Australian property as several distinct regional cycles, not one homogeneous market.
Commodities / Western Australia Bullish Macro 00:28:20
  • WA property and broader WA economic conditions linked directly to the ongoing commodities bull-market thesis discussed in prior sessions.
  • Positioned as a structural, longer-term tailwind rather than a near-term trade.
  • Consumer-facing/resource-heavy regions seen as better positioned than the more expensive east-coast markets.

Session Themes

  • Rising government debt, persistent inflation and elevated asset prices are steadily eroding the traditional "study, work, buy a house, retire" pathway — Tung frames this as a gradual deterioration rather than one dramatic event.
  • Governments "kicking the can down the road" on fiscal deficits shows up later as inflation, currency debasement and higher asset prices rather than a distant future crisis.
  • People are responding to the affordability squeeze through different "tribes": geo-arbitrage (~00:31:22, e.g. Dubai, Malaysia, regional Italy), the manosphere (~00:35:56, work harder/build skills), the trad-wife movement (single-income households), van life/tiny homes (~00:37:25, reducing housing capital requirements), and Gen Z disengagement — Japan's "Satori Generation" (~01:02:32) and China's "tang ping"/lying flat.
  • Macro analysis identifies structural opportunities/risks and valuation extremes; technical analysis (as taught by Craig, Jamie and David) supplies the timing — the two are presented as complementary, not substitutes.
  • Core actionable takeaway: individuals can't control government debt, inflation or monetary policy, but can control financial education, spending, career positioning, geographic flexibility and active capital allocation/rotation.
  • Tung shared that losing roughly half his net worth in the 2008 financial crisis is what drove him to study how macro forces flow through to individual wealth — framed as a risk-management lesson, not a prediction exercise.

Session Themes

  • Market structure over prediction: bearish/bullish divergence is a warning, not a signal — Craig repeatedly stresses waiting for an actual break of structure (a failed higher high or a broken prior low) before changing bias, across indices, tech, Bitcoin and individual stocks.

  • Market had been primed for higher grades after the initial discovery hole (23 July: 6m at 7g/t, 3m at 12g/t, 10m at 3g/t, 5m at 5g/t) plus a large 59m visual sulfide zone — so this update disappointed relative to inflated expectations.

  • Craig's view: not a bad announcement at all — builds the case that the deposit has enough scale to feed current processing and could support expanding throughput (15k → 20-30k tpa) over the next 1-2 years.
  • Frames the sell-off as a buying opportunity created by mismatched market expectations rather than deterioration in the underlying asset.
ATH Bullish FA 00:55:07
  • Developing a drug for multiple system atrophy (MSA, related to Parkinson's).
  • Phase 2 (randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial plus an open-label arm in advanced patients) showed the 50mg dose consistently beating both placebo and the 75mg dose across every disease-progression marker.
  • FDA has now confirmed acceptance of the proposed Phase 3 program design, closely replicating the successful Phase 2 protocol (200 patients, 50mg twice daily, 12 months).
  • Trial slated to start toward the end of the year; ~$37m cash on hand, but a year-long Phase 3 is expensive — a funding partner/JV or commercial prepayment deal (rather than a standard dilutive raise) is possible.
  • Market cap ~$100-120m, which Craig calls "not very demanding" for a company about to enter Phase 3 with a well-funded, high-value catalyst — flagged to revisit in October for trial-start progress and any partnership news.
PDN (Paladin Energy / uranium pricing) Neutral FA 00:09:32
  • William asked how Paladin can report selling uranium at $70 when reported/futures pricing looks higher.
  • Craig's core educational point: uranium spot price (only ~20% of the market, dominated by traders/speculators) is a poor guide to the real uranium market — "ignore it" for fundamental analysis; useful only for short-term sentiment trades.
  • Long-term contract pricing (the other ~80% of the market) has climbed steadily from ~$25 (2017) to ~$95 now, and is the metric that actually matters to producers and utilities.
  • PDN's ~$70 pricing reflects contracts struck a couple of years ago at lower prevailing prices; new contracts should price higher.
  • Some contracts have floor/ceiling mechanisms linking partially to spot moves, but long-term contract relationships give producers pricing certainty and easier access to financing.

Session Themes

  • Uranium market structure 101: why spot price is misleading and long-term contract pricing is the real signal to watch for uranium producers.
  • FA "cheat sheet" pushback: Craig dismissed an AI-generated list of financial ratios as impractical, reiterating his preference for a small curated toolkit (PE, forward PE, gross/net margin, debt/equity, free cash flow) over exhaustive traditional ratio analysis, especially since 60-75% of the ASX isn't profitable.
  • Geological risk in mining (using BOE as a cautionary example): resources can disappoint post-drilling when companies believe their own story without stress-testing it, or drill to "just enough" for JORC categories rather than to high confidence.
  • Recurring earnings-season theme (EDV, FLT): revenue growth isn't the same as profit growth — rising costs eating into conversion/margin is the real challenge for several companies reporting this period.
  • Market overreactions create opportunities: both the EDV commentary and the PGO trading-halt sell-off were framed as cases where mismatched expectations, not underlying deterioration, drove share-price weakness.

  • September is the key risk window: Core PCE, Fed communication, the September FOMC (~15–16 Sep) and the Bank of Japan decision (17 Sep) — Craig is using current strength to selectively take profit and reduce exposure ahead of these, not to call a top.
  • Elliott Wave degree/proportionality was a recurring teaching point — a lower-degree pullback shouldn't be judged against a higher-degree correction's depth or duration; rule of alternation (sharp wave 2 often means complex/sideways wave 4).
  • Commodities remain the strongest structural theme: gold structurally bullish, copper's long-term supply/demand thesis intact despite near-term divergence, energy weakness viewed as accumulation within a multi-year electricity-demand thesis, uranium in early public-participation stages, and agricultural commodities increasingly breaking out.
  • Distinguish what you actually own within a theme — producer vs developer vs explorer (uranium) or commodity ETF vs operating business (agriculture) carry very different risk/return profiles for the same macro thesis.
  • Market structure and volume confirmation matter more than picking exact bottoms — DroneShield near support is still technically bearish; Chalice/Phoenix are showing early structural improvement but await volume/level confirmation.
  • Craig stressed staying adaptive — his BHP view was revised once copper strength and liquidity conditions changed; technical counts are probability frameworks, not fixed predictions.

Session Themes

  • Broad-based improvement in the Australian market, particularly commodities, resources and small caps, following a difficult Feb–Jul corrective period.
  • "Red doesn't mean wrong" — a decline or bearish candle doesn't automatically invalidate a trade; market structure, volume, support zones and the original thesis determine validity, not candle colour.
  • Zig/zag framework repeated throughout: strong advances are expected to have substantial corrections, which become opportunities when they terminate at logical technical areas with buyers regaining control.
  • Asymmetric returns matter — a handful of 10:1–12:1 winners (e.g. SRVM) can materially drive portfolio performance; don't cap exceptional trades early.
  • Position sizing discipline — if ordinary 30–60% corrections in volatile small caps feel intolerable, exposure is likely too large; capital preservation through drawdowns is what allows traders to benefit when trends resume.
  • Distinguish thesis invalidation (a defined technical level breaking) from temporary discomfort/emotion; traders can exit and re-enter — holding purely on hope creates unnecessary risk.
  • Earnings/event risk: without sufficient profit buffer ahead of an announcement, Dave prefers to close the position rather than risk an unpredictable gap.
  • Market bottoms often form amid maximum pessimism; commodity-related small caps completing corrections and breaking higher is seen as evidence the recent precious-metals/uranium weakness was a bottom rather than an interim rally.

Session Themes

  • End-of-earnings-season theme: with most results out, investors have a fresh dataset, but the key skill is separating genuinely new information from what markets already priced in via quarterly/trading updates (VEA especially)
  • Recurring caution around promotional language in ASX announcements — "discovery" vs "extension," and misleading distance/scale framing (RML)
  • Drilling-purpose framework: distinguishing discovery drilling from resource-extension, confidence-upgrade, and geological-model-validation drilling (AGE, White Cliff)
  • Sustainability of "exceptional" earnings vs a durable trend — Viva Energy's refining windfall and Woodside's pricing-driven beat both flagged as needing scrutiny of what happens once conditions normalise
  • Commodity price cycle timing driving development urgency (TGN racing to capture the current tungsten price window before prices normalise toward 2030)
  • Balance-sheet discipline: DBI's high debt/low liquidity flagged as a constraint despite a "safe" infrastructure asset profile
  • ASX companies can stop mandatory quarterly reporting once granted relief after 4 quarters of positive operating cash flow, leading to long newsflow gaps for mature companies

Session Themes

Session Themes

  • Define the purpose of a position (short-term trade vs. swing vs. long-term investment) before entering, and manage it according to that original objective — the same stock can be simultaneously overbought on the daily and attractive on the three-monthly
  • "Don't trade every butterfly" — small retracements inside a larger trend rarely hit exact Fibonacci levels; over-trading corrections in long-term holdings risks missing the larger move
  • Small, controlled losses preserve the ability to participate in the eventual large winning move (illustrated via CSL's repeated stopped-out attempts)
  • Separate trading and investment accounts to keep timeframe and mindset aligned with each position's purpose
  • Position size according to conviction, asset quality, liquidity and risk — not just upside potential (Beach Energy sized much smaller than Woodside/Santos)
  • Multi-timeframe approach: use monthly/quarterly charts to locate the macro cycle, then zoom into lower timeframes to define entries and invalidation
  • Preferred confirmation sequence for turning points: buying → liquidity sweep → renewed buying at a higher level → change in market structure
  • Commodity cycle sequencing: precious metals lead, then industrial metals, then energy, then soft commodities — oil/energy viewed as the current laggard with catch-up potential (oil above ~$120, energy sector above ~12,000 flagged as major confirmation levels)
  • Psychological emphasis on patience, matching chart-checking frequency to intended holding period, and building conviction from understanding the macro cycle rather than hope

  • BHP previously assessed and passed on a NexGen deal; a recent land purchase near Rook 1 keeps it in the frame (see NexGen Energy below).
NexGen Energy Neutral FA 00:11:49
  • Reported BHP/NexGen "talks" are not evidence of a transaction — BHP already ran the ruler over a deal last year and didn't proceed.
  • NexGen needs at least ~$1bn more over the next ~9 months to advance Rook 1; a deal could look like a strategic stake with capital injection, though Craig doubts BHP would settle for a small minority position.
  • Views the publicised "talks" partly as a negotiating tactic to pressure other financiers into acting — drew a parallel to Vault Minerals' takeover interest forcing Genesis Minerals to move.
  • Bottom line: strategically plausible but no real information yet; wait for concrete terms rather than trading the speculation.
SPZ (Smart Parking) Bullish FA 00:17:41
  • One of the best results reviewed today: revenue +63%, adjusted EBITDA +50%, underlying adjusted NPAT +73%, with ~$17m cash on hand.
  • UK overheads rose only ~5% while UK revenue grew 60%+ and EBITDA +50% — clear operating leverage, unlike other recent names where costs scaled alongside revenue.
  • Further upside seen from US expansion runway, growing contribution from recent acquisitions, and tech deployment (smart/cloud) to lift margins on existing assets.
  • Caution: multi-country expansion adds regulatory/tax/operational complexity, and further acquisitions could require capital beyond the current $17m cash balance.
  • Called "one of the better results that I've seen today," deserving of the share-price move it got.

AGE Bullish FA 00:32:22

CPR Neutral FA 00:34:34

RR1 Bullish FA 00:38:01

GMG (Goodman Group) Neutral FA 00:41:44

  • Framed as a strategic/thematic observation rather than a specific trade call — one to watch as the model plays out over the coming years.
AUC (Ausgold) / OceanaGold Neutral FA 00:46:10
  • OceanaGold's offer values Ausgold at ~$1.36/share (~2.44Moz resource, ~1.3Moz reserve, ~120koz targeted annual production) — a ~20-25% premium to the recent share price, not an outstanding premium but "gets the job done."
  • Holder options: hold and receive 0.03365 OceanaGold shares per AUC share, sell on market (trading close to the $1.36 equivalent), or elect for a partial cash offer (allocation not guaranteed, scales with total elections).

SVL (Silver Mines) Neutral FA 00:49:18
  • Project has been stuck in a ~2-year court/permitting process; management's repeated confidence hasn't translated into resolution, and no clear timeline was given in the latest update (an earlier reference point had suggested a possible decision around November 2026).
  • New DFS uses a conservative base-case silver price of US$35-40/oz — economics are "workable" but not exceptional at that level; cash generation improves materially near US$60/oz and becomes strong above ~US$80/oz.
  • CapEx has risen significantly versus the prior 2024 study, by close to $200m including stage 2, driven by inflation and an extended mine life from a larger resource; flagged that the DFS headline uses pre-tax figures and doesn't disclose deposit grade — worth checking further.
  • View: attracts silver-name buying interest, but permitting/court risk remains the dominant issue — better suited to trading silver sentiment/momentum than a long-term position until the legal process resolves; financing (offtake/streaming/debt) would be readily available if it clears.

Session Themes

  • Interpreting earnings/announcements relative to what the market already expects, not just whether the headline looks good or bad (BHP, SPZ; Domino's/CSL/Cochlear used as the "stability after prolonged bad news" framework for turnarounds).
  • Distinguishing capital raisings that fund genuine value creation (TNC, AGE) from dilution for its own sake — judge raises by what they unlock.
  • De-risking events (RR1's funding partner, Ausgold's acquisition by OceanaGold) can matter more than resource or production growth headlines.
  • Separating exploration process from discovery — geophysical anomalies (CPR) are targeting tools, not proof of mineralisation.
  • Reading feasibility studies beyond the headline number: pre-tax vs post-tax presentation, grade disclosure, and commodity price assumptions (SVL).
  • Corporate actions like share consolidations (HGO/Kantra) and commodity hedging can create technical price pressure independent of underlying fundamentals.
  • Community-oriented infrastructure is increasingly used to help large industrial developments (e.g., GMG data centres) win planning and community support.

CSL Neutral FA 00:01:56

COH (Cochlear) Neutral FA 00:04:10 (revisited in depth at 00:54:27)

BOE (Boss Energy) Neutral FA 00:10:43

  • Real reason for the redesign: the areas BOE can still access are lower grade, and the current well design can't economically recover uranium there — original resource/mine-plan modelling was flawed.
  • Genuine positive: mine is already producing (5 ramped-up columns, hit revised FY26 guidance) with ~$50m cash on hand — a real base to build from.
  • Craig expects the study to conclude the redesign is "economically viable," but stresses it won't be "the mine everyone paid for."
  • FY27 guidance due alongside the study — key for assessing forward cost structure and cash flow, including possible extra debt needs.
  • Craig's stance: a positive study could still push the stock higher on narrative, but traders need to understand the underlying grade/resource risk before treating this as a clean re-rate.
QML (QMines) Bullish FA 00:27:13
  • Strong hit: 35m at ~3% copper — a notably higher-grade pocket within the deposit.
  • ~10,000m of infill drilling underway in the pit (using a lake-mounted rig, since the pit has water) for metallurgical work and grade control.
  • DFS still on track for the next few months; metal price assumptions used are ~2 years old, so expect the updated DFS to show higher revenue assumptions offsetting CapEx inflation.
  • Sulfur by-product pricing outlook is also favourable and will be incorporated into the DFS.
  • Craig's take: one of the best copper projects on the ASX — will feature in his upcoming copper-themed content.

PAR (Paradigm Biopharmaceuticals) Bullish FA 00:32:32
  • Phase 3 trial ongoing; independent Data Safety Monitoring Board has completed its 3rd safety check and cleared the trial to continue.
  • Key upcoming catalyst: interim analysis due September 2026 — a "go/no-go" read on whether the drug is showing the desired effect, though not confirmatory of final Phase 3 results.
  • Timeline flagged back in an earlier August check-in is still intact.
  • Craig frames it as exactly the type of high-value catalyst play they look for, while cautioning that positive interim signals don't guarantee the final Phase 3 outcome (bigger/longer trials can regress).
LAM (Laramide Resources) Neutral FA 00:35:51
  • Uranium developer; flagship Westmoreland-area project sits in Queensland, which currently bans uranium mining, so the project can't advance for now.
  • Thesis: a recent Indian government delegation and India's nuclear build-out could eventually pressure Australia/Queensland to reconsider the ban.

BHM (Broken Hill Mines) Bullish FA 00:42:15
  • New discovery confirmed at "Centenary," beneath the main lodes in the western mining area, with solid zinc/lead/silver-equivalent grades.
  • Craig sees this as a positive read for mine-life extension given proximity to existing mining infrastructure.
  • Production mix expected to show more silver coming through over the next 1–2 quarters as new mining areas ramp up.
  • Additional shallow high-grade hits at Pinnacles (RASP mining area) could lift the blended grade profile — current silver grades run only ~40–90g/t.
  • Rising silver price would amplify the profitability upside if these higher-grade zones get incorporated.
EGA Neutral FA 00:44:53
  • Spin-out from Pure Hydrogen; first drilling since listing is now underway (Venus 2 well).
  • This is the first horizontal well ever drilled in this gas field — designed to punch through the existing Venus 1 well to access more of the coal seam and improve flow rates.
  • Drilling expected to take ~14 days; an announcement on completion/intersection could land within about a week of this call.
  • Craig flags heavy retail anticipation after years of these assets sitting undrilled — an important read not just for EGA but for the wider field.
EOS Neutral FA 00:47:29
  • Market cap pushing toward ~$2b, riding the defense/counter-drone thematic.
  • Order book at $846m, up 84% in 6 months — strong even excluding the recent Mars acquisition (a command-and-control counter-drone system).
  • FY26 revenue guidance raised from $242–270m to $280–300m; underlying EBITDA expected to turn positive in H1 2026.
  • Risk flagged clearly by Craig: the valuation is being driven by growth narrative/thematic, not current profits — EOS still isn't making money, and if order momentum slows, the stock is vulnerable to a sharp de-rate.

Session Themes

  • How to value a capital raise properly: Craig walked through LSR's May raise as a case study — discount ($900k) + auction value ($1.8m) + broker shares ($900k) + broker options ($900k) + broker fees ($280k) added up to ~$4m given away, ~85% of the raise's total value, with current holders only netting ~15% benefit from the funds raised. Reinforces why strong entries before a raise matter.
  • Uranium sector deep-dive: BOE, LOT and LAM all covered in the same session, spanning production risk, recovery signs, and a policy-driven developer thesis.
  • FY26 reporting season framework: both CSL and Cochlear show the market currently rewarding "stability confirmed" over "growth," a lens Craig said applies broadly to large caps reporting this season.
  • Defense/counter-drone thematic momentum continues to re-rate EOS, but Craig repeatedly flagged that the valuation has outrun current profitability.
  • Content roadmap: a Copper-themed video/live session is next (voted ahead of Silver), with a Silver video (covering names like SBL/BML) to follow.
  • Trading psychology callout: praised a community member for cutting a loss quickly once the "thesis broke" — reinforcing discipline and consistent strategy execution over P&L-watching.

Macro Sunday

Hosted by Tung Nguyen | Sunday 16 August 2026
Bullish Setups: Gold, Value Stocks (multi-year rotation thesis)

Telcos Bearish Macro 00:39:02
  • Explicit sector call: bearish telcos despite them normally fitting his "value stock" bucket.
  • Trigger is Starlink/satellite internet as a long-term disruptive threat — cited Elon Musk comments on Starlink in every car, plus Malaysian telcos already partnering with Starlink for distribution ("letting the wolf into the hen house").
  • As satellite antennas miniaturise (10-15 year horizon), sees SIM cards and cell tower infrastructure becoming obsolete, comparing telcos' position to Blockbuster facing Netflix with no real competitive response available.
  • Broke down telco revenue risk: ~24-25% from fixed broadband (highest risk), ~42% from mobile data (moderate risk now, but up to 67% of income at risk once handset-sized satellite antennas arrive.

  • Framed via the recurring theme that the best-performing asset class of the next 10 years is unlikely to be the same as the last 10 years — with markets at valuation extremes last seen at the dot-com peak and the Great Depression, sees conditions ripe for capital to rotate back into value.
  • Tied to a broader passive-vs-active investing point: passive/DCA investing looks easy in a one-way bull market, but picking pockets of strength (commodities, precious metals, energy, uranium, and likely value stocks going forward) will matter more in a harder, sideways/bear environment.
  • Highlighted a JPMorgan positioning chart showing USD-bullish contract positioning at all-time highs (~2 standard deviations, top ~2-3% of readings).
  • Reads this as a contrarian warning flag given the backdrop of a structural US fiscal deficit, rising interest costs, and "Ponzi scheme"-like debt dynamics (per the Michael Burry clip played) — called the extreme bullishness "ballsy."
  • Not calling an imminent USD top: notes there's no obvious rotation destination (Euro, yuan and ruble all far behind USD's ~60% share of global trade), so expects USD dominance to persist longer than the bear case would suggest, with only "small pockets" of capital (himself included) rotating into gold, and increasing private/corporate — not central bank — flows into Bitcoin.

  • No explicit short/sell call — framed as a risk to be positioned for rather than an imminent trade.
  • Interest paid on 30-year Treasuries is at its highest level since 2009 — read as a clear signal of US economic/fiscal stress and rising cost of capital for both government and business borrowing.
  • Connected to a broader "canary in the coal mine" picture: credit card delinquencies are back at GFC-era levels, with student loan and auto loan delinquencies also spiking, while mortgage delinquencies remain comparatively resilient.
  • Net interest on federal debt is now the 3rd-largest US budget line (behind Social Security/Medicare), exceeding total national defense spending — flagged as structurally unsustainable given fixed costs (Medicare, Social Security, defense, veterans benefits) are all still rising.
  • Central macro risk being tracked: if the BoJ has to raise rates sharply to defend the yen, the global yen carry trade (cheap JPY borrowing funneled into US Treasuries, FAANG/AI stocks and property) would have to unwind, forcing sales of those assets to repatriate yen — a broad-based asset-price-decline trigger.
  • Cited an unverified (translated, purportedly BoJ-insider) social post warning of major measures coming and referencing 2026 specifically — treated explicitly as an unconfirmed rumour/"pre micro sign," not a confirmed signal, but flagged as worth watching for confirming data.
  • Reiterated his personal framework here: macro calls are reliably early (referenced Michael Burry positioning 2 years ahead of the 2008 GFC), so the point isn't to time it exactly but to stay positioned so the portfolio survives (ideally thrives) if/when it plays out.

Session Themes

  • Opened with an extended geo-arbitrage/travel segment from Penang, Malaysia (cost of living, expat community, "fat FIRE arbitrage" concept of upgrading lifestyle rather than just banking savings) and a cautionary macro parable via Kelly's Castle — a Scottish merchant who over-leveraged, over-capitalised into a non-income-producing asset, and was wiped out by a commodity (coffee) price slump and a flu outbreak among his workers, dying before finishing the house.
  • Core teaching frame: cause-and-effect chains across the PESTEL framework (political → economic → social → legal, etc.) — illustrated with a worked example (Iran/Middle East conflict → oil supply shock → inflation → rate hikes → reduced household spending → recession) as the template for macro reasoning.
  • Global sovereign debt stress as the session's central thread: rising rates are sharply increasing interest costs everywhere, most acutely in Japan (debt/GDP ~240-250% vs US ~120% and Australia ~30s%) given its near-zero rate history; described the current dynamic as "using one credit card to pay off another."
  • US tariff policy assessed as a failure on its own terms: tariff revenue was meant to help pay down debt, but US debt has grown from ~$37T to ~$40T since, a US Supreme Court ruling forced ~$100B in "Liberation Day" tariff refunds, and customs duties have fallen for three straight months (May-July) — creating disputes over whether refunded tariffs get passed back to end payers or kept as windfalls by intermediaries.
  • K-shaped US economy: average headline data (unemployment, GDP) looks fine, but a Bloomberg survey of 75 economists predicting July job growth was wrong (jobs fell ~23k), and government spending's share of GDP has risen from ~23% (2010s) to ~26% — alongside sharply rising credit card/auto/student-loan delinquencies concentrated in the bottom of the K.
  • Referenced a Jamie Dimon clip on rising geopolitical/military competition (China's dominance in drones, EVs, batteries, solar, shipbuilding) as context for why US military spending is set to keep rising, adding further pressure to the deficit.
  • Recurring meta-theme: "the best-performing asset of the next 10 years is unlikely to be the best-performing asset of the last 10 years" — applied across value stocks, tech/AI, USD, and telcos — alongside the reminder that macro-driven calls are consistently early, so the goal is portfolio positioning/survival rather than precise timing.
  • Ran out of time to cover Asia/Australia-specific charts this session; flagged for a future call.

Session Themes

  • Opened with a psychology segment (using his daughter learning to ride a bike as the analogy) on embracing the difficulty of the learning curve — most profitable traders had a genuinely hard journey, not an overnight one, and hard-won skills carry more lasting satisfaction/resilience than easy ones.
  • Repeated "zig-zag / zag zone" framework applied consistently across almost every chart: a strong move (zig) needs a healthy retracement (zag) bought by returning buyers to confirm trend continuation; failure to attract buyers on the zag is the tell for a change of market structure.
  • "Take out the high, take out the low" liquidity-sweep pattern highlighted repeatedly (Technology/XIJ, DXY, Uranium, Oil, Woodside) as one of the highest risk-reward setups to watch in both directions (as a buy and as a distribution/sell signal).
  • Contrarian sentiment framework reinforced via the AUDUSD/gold example — when comment-section sentiment is heavily one-sided, that's often the setup for the opposite move; tied back to the AAII-style sentiment gauge shown at the top of the call.
  • Ratios explained via a Q&A (framed through a BHP/AUD example): all asset prices are implicitly ratios, and professional analysis focuses on relative strength between assets (e.g. gold vs Dow, Bitcoin vs gold/Nasdaq) rather than isolated USD/AUD price charts.
  • Long-term investing guidance repeated across copper, silver and precious metals: don't try to time the exact bottom on genuine multi-year/decade theses — scale in gradually (e.g. staged buys/DCA) once price is clearly in an accumulation or early-bull zone, since waiting for a "perfect" low risks missing the move entirely.
  • Cross-asset caution flagged around AU/US 10-year yields breaking higher as a potential headwind for rate-sensitive assets (Property/XPJ, Technology/XIJ) and a tailwind for the AUD and financials.
  • Reiterated a personal risk-management rule: never hold a position through a change of market structure against the position, regardless of tax or conviction — always close and re-enter if the data changes (referenced closing TCL and part of a Bitcoin position for this reason).

Session Themes

  • Elliott Wave counts are frequently ambiguous - the desk openly carried 2-4 competing counts (gold, cotton, XJO) with defined invalidation levels rather than a single "correct" answer, and stressed waiting for price to confirm rather than forcing a narrative.
  • Repeated emphasis on confluence: combining Elliott Wave structure with RSI divergence (regular vs hidden, bullish vs bearish), volume/OBV analysis, anchored VWAP, volume-profile point of control, and Fibonacci retracement/extension levels to build higher-conviction entries.
  • Volume (OBV) as a truth-test for price moves - repeatedly used to flag moves that "aren't being supported" (Ramelius, Brambles, WiseTech) versus moves with genuine participation (Evolution, Origin, Sims).
  • Macro-cycle framing (accumulation → public participation → excess phases, within larger cycles/super-cycles) applied across uranium, AI hardware, and individual ASX names to contextualise where in a multi-year trend a stock currently sits.
  • "Gold leads, everything else follows" - precious metals direction treated as the swing factor for related plays (Zimplats/platinum, broader materials sector).
  • Liquidity/ICT concepts (fair value gaps, order blocks, wick sweeps, strong vs weak highs/lows) used alongside Elliott Wave for entries (referenced for HYPE, oil, gold) - flagged as a deep separate discipline outside the core curriculum.
  • Distinguishing a strong operational/technical setup from an investable entry: several names (Santos, WiseTech, Brambles, CSL) had constructive structure but were flagged as "not yet" trades pending a confirmed breakout, volume support, or an earnings catalyst.

Gold / Silver Neutral FA 00:00:44
  • Opened noting gold and silver "heading back" / pulling back; asked if members caught a short on the move.
  • Framed as a possible pullback (small or large) rather than a change of trend - "the long term thesis is still perfectly fine."
  • Used as a teaching moment on taking profits into strength and re-entering later - selling into strength doesn't mean abandoning the thesis, and pullbacks can offer a discount for those with long-term conviction in specific names.
  • General reminder: the market usually gives more than one entry opportunity - no need to force a hold through every drawdown.
DroneShield (DRO) Neutral FA 00:04:09
  • Responding to a member (Penny) question about a large pre-market cross trade and whether it signalled "smart money" buying.
  • Large trades well outside normal hours are more likely cross trades: transfers between funds, negotiated deals between large holders, or securities-lending arrangements - not automatically accumulation.
  • Checked substantial-holder notices from the same window: two notices (JPMorgan Chase and Citibank) referenced securities held/loaned "subject to an obligation to return" - consistent with short-interest/securities-lending activity, not straightforward buying.
  • Practical takeaway: always check substantial-holder notices after an unusually large cross trade to determine if it's short-related, a fund-to-fund transfer, or a genuine holder change.
TKM Bearish FA 00:07:15
  • Addressed a member (Sam) question about TKM's manganese assay results and share-price reaction.
  • Share price had run hard on ~60% manganese rock-chip results; rock chips are not representative of an eventual deposit-average grade, so the run was seen as unsupported ("a table without legs").
  • Follow-up drill assays (44%, 34%, 24%, 19%) came in below the rock-chip-driven expectations; ~19% is low grade, mid-20s is transitional low/medium - only the top result is arguably high grade, so headline "high grade" framing is misleading.
  • Sell-off considered justified given the disconnect between priced-in expectations and actual results, and technicals (RSI/momentum) were already flagged as weak before the drop.
  • Not judged a bad result operationally - a solid maiden-drill outcome that supports further exploration - just a mismatch between company-level success and share-price expectations.
  • Watch item: consistency of the next round of assays from the same drill program, not just the headline numbers.
RML Neutral FA 00:15:37
  • Addressed a member (Chrissy) question comparing RML to a peer antimony/tungsten name referred to on the call as "84" (ticker unclear from the transcript audio).
  • Market caps are close (~$140m vs ~$100m), but the peer recently acquired a refinery - a major, costly but strategically significant deal that puts it well ahead of RML in processing capability.
  • RML will likely intersect known antimony/tungsten mineralisation given the area's established mineralisation, but that does not confirm an economic deposit - too early to compare deposit quality directly.
  • Despite positive US critical-minerals policy tailwinds (FAST-41 designation, defense industrial base consortium), still years away from actual antimony production.
  • Conclusion: RML looks overvalued relative to the peer once the peer's refinery acquisition is factored in - value already priced in versus development stage reached.
LUX Neutral FA 00:20:04
  • Addressed a member (Annaliese) question on a newly IPO'd copper explorer in Alaska's Ambler district.
  • Very limited trading history (~1 month of candles) makes technical analysis largely unusable at this stage - fundamentals have to carry the assessment.
  • Historic (pre-IPO) drilling included strong intercepts (e.g. 37m at 2.45% copper) plus a promising zinc/polymetallic prospect with silver and lead credits - genuinely interesting geology, backed by an experienced team (ex-S2 Resources/Red 5 personnel).
  • At a ~$40m market cap, however, considerable exploration success and excitement is already priced in - would be more interesting nearer a $15-20m cap.
  • Watching for geophysics and the maiden diamond-drill program (visuals could move the market); the more attractive entry would likely come if the stock pulls back below its IPO price once more data is available.
Galan Lithium (GLN) Bullish FA 00:27:47
  • Progressing well through commissioning/ramp-up of its brine project; concentrate is now flowing through the plant with a "so far, so far, it's doing pretty well" ramp-up.
  • First commercial product sales guided to end of this year (not month-to-month), with roughly 4 months of ramp-up risk still to navigate.
  • The earlier development pause during weak lithium prices left ~70% of construction and the evaporation ponds already built, giving a head start (concentrated brine inventory) into the 4,000-to-5,200-tonne expansion, which needs no new plant capacity.
  • Grade advantage: GLN's brine grade is described as notably better than most other ASX-listed brine developers, aiding project economics.
  • Explicit contrast drawn with AGY (Argosy Minerals), whose ramp-up went wrong and left it stuck for ~3 years - GLN's more cautious, staged approach (get the plant running, then expand) is viewed as the right sequencing and is "paying off... so far."
  • Key near-term watch item: the nanofiltration plant continuing to run to spec and scale over the next 3-4 months.
Catalyst Metals (CYL) Neutral FA 00:34:45
  • Addressed a member (Chris) question prompted by heavy broker/influencer promotion of the stock.
  • Strong track record acknowledged: turned around the loss-making Plutonic operation (acquired ~3 years ago) into 4 operating mines (from 1 a year ago), ~104,000oz production, AISC ~A$2,750/oz, and built ~$331m cash while spending ~$300m on mine builds, plant refurbishment and its own power plant.
  • Targeting ~2 million ounce reserves and ~200,000oz per annum production, with Old Highway and Cinnamon mines still to come online over the next 6-18 months.
  • Valuation question is the crux: "~$1.6bn... I'm not sure I don't really think so" - execution has been excellent, but whether that's fully priced in is unresolved; flagged as "definitely one to have on your list" rather than a value opportunity.
  • Open question for the story beyond the current mine plan: what's the next growth leg once the current targets are hit - no clear line of sight yet.
Lithium Argentina (LAR) Neutral FA 00:43:27
  • Addressed a member (Brian) question; NYSE/TSX-listed (not ASX), holding a 44% interest in an operating lithium-carbonate project in Argentina, with genuine joint decision-making rights (not a passive stake).
  • Recent positive cash flow driven mainly by carbonate pricing strength rather than volume growth; contrasted favourably with IGO's underperforming carbonate conversion facility.
  • Stage 2 expansion (+45,000 tpa) planned, incorporating modular Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) - technology "not proven at scale," so treated as a genuine execution risk/unknown rather than a given.
  • ~$100m cash plus an undrawn debt facility; considering an ASX listing - open question (flagged as one to watch) is whether that capital gets deployed into the existing project or into a new Australian asset.
  • Valued essentially only on its project interest, not on any broader asset base.
Core Lithium (CXO) Neutral FA 00:48:59
  • Addressed a member (Hayden) question on the BP33 drill result (34m at 2% lithium) - confirmed as a genuinely good result (above the ~1% general and ~1.5-2% underground-specific grade thresholds).
  • Caution flagged: the imminent "first shipment" news is remnant ore from the Grants open pit during plant/flow-sheet commissioning, not a sign that full mining has resumed.
  • Real underground BP33 mining is not expected until at least mid-next-year, with steady-state operation potentially not until mid-2028 or later - a multi-year journey, not a 6-month turnaround.
  • Company holds a solid liquidity buffer, which management will likely need given how often companies in this stage of ramp-up have had to raise capital again.
  • Any further strength in lithium pricing would ease the path, but the timeline caution stands regardless.
SGQ Bearish FA 00:52:12
  • Addressed a member (Lucas) question on the recent Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) - a genuinely good project result: increased tonnage, better measured & indicated (higher-confidence) resource, and favourable (flat, near-surface) mining geometry.
  • Despite the good result, the share price has been rolling over as the "fast money" that piled in on discovery-phase excitement exits now that a major uncertainty (deposit scale) has been resolved - a recognised, repeatable pattern in the resource sector.
  • Still carries a large valuation (~$450m market cap) with claims of grades/tonnages rivalling Mountain Pass and Mount Weld, but is a long way from production - metallurgical test work to separate niobium from the mixed rare-earth by-product stream is described as the critical "go/no-go" step, with a scoping study not expected until toward year-end.
  • Expectation stated explicitly: "this drifts and eventually drifts a bit further back down" as the story transitions from discovery excitement into the slower economic-study phase.
Lodestar Minerals (LSR) Neutral FA 00:58:11
  • Addressed a member (Gallon) question on why the market ignored LSR's "high grade" headline results.
  • Verdict: the headline is not accurate - it reflects gram-metres (grade x intercept width), not genuine high grams-per-tonne grade, so the muted market reaction was the correct response.
  • Positive: management is moving relatively quickly toward a potential mining permit next year.
  • Negative: far too little drilling/geological data currently exists to assess whether a coherent, economic deposit is actually there - "we just don't know" what the mineralisation could look like at this stage.
  • General reminder to the room: know approximate low/medium/high grade ranges for each commodity (gold, silver, copper, antimony, PGMs, lithium, rare earths) rather than trusting headline wording, since grade language can be "massaged."

Session Themes

  • Distinguishing a good geological/operational result from a good share-price catalyst - repeatedly, strong results (TKM's drilling, SGQ's MRE, Core Lithium's BP33 intercept) didn't justify a higher share price because expectations were already priced in or excitement had already peaked.
  • Project-stage literacy: rock chips are not drilling, drilling is not a resource, a resource is not a mine - each transition needs more evidence before it can be valued the same way (explicitly applied to TKM, LUX, RML, SGQ, LSR, CXO).
  • Interpreting unusual large trades via substantial-holder notices to distinguish accumulation from securities lending/short activity (DroneShield example).
  • "Fast money vs slow money" in resource stocks - explains why share prices can fall even on genuinely good news once the phase that attracted speculative capital ends (SGQ).
  • Grade literacy across commodities - knowing approximate low/medium/high ranges (manganese, lithium, gram-metres vs g/t) rather than trusting promotional headline language (TKM, LSR).
  • Execution track record vs valuation - strong operators (Galan, Catalyst Metals) can still raise a legitimate "is this priced in" question distinct from "are they good operators."
  • Psychology of trading pullbacks: taking profit into strength doesn't mean losing the thesis - the market tends to offer a second entry, reducing the pressure to hold every position through every drawdown.

Market Mornings

Hosted by Craig Dickson | Tuesday 11 August 2026
Bullish Setups: LGM, TGM, AKA, ARO, SPD

LGM Bullish FA 00:09:33

ARO Bullish FA 00:29:54

SPD Bullish FA 00:43:30

Life360 Bearish FA 00:37:06

  • No corresponding upgrade to subscription revenue or adjusted EBITDA guidance despite the strong headline growth — a clear signal incremental revenue isn't converting into incremental profit.
  • Craig's framework: premium/growth companies need operating leverage (revenue growing faster than costs); when costs outpace revenue growth instead, that's "a terrible look" regardless of how good the top-line numbers appear.
SRL Bearish FA 00:50:28
  • Explicit answer to "is there still value in SRL?": "No. No there's not" — even though SRL remains the clear scandium sector leader and the US government interest is a genuine vote of confidence.
  • Market cap has run to ~$2.7B against a mid-case project NPV of only ~US$890M (~A$1.5B) — directly compared to the earlier IPT titanium project, where market cap similarly outran NPV before the DFS caused a collapse.
  • A conditional (not yet confirmed) ~US$400M US Dept. of War loan would push the project from a simple NSW mine + basic refining operation into a materially more complex, higher-risk build — including new US-based downstream chemical-grade scandium refining capacity.

BHL Neutral FA 00:06:47

AR1 Neutral FA 00:15:51

  • Longer-term, the acquired ground could still prove useful if AR1 finds more than what Hammer itself discovered.

HWK Neutral FA 00:18:57

  • Latest results are visual observations plus handheld spot-reader copper ranges, not lab assays over defined intervals — explicitly flagged as encouraging but not reliable evidence; some historical data also comes from RAB drilling, a technique prone to sample contamination.
  • No resource yet; Craig doesn't expect one before 2027, pending lab assays and further drilling programs.
EVR Neutral FA 00:26:46
  • Testing a "hub-and-spoke" antimony model: paying artisanal miners a small upfront amount (~12-12.5%) for stockpiled ore, processing it through a small plant, with the balance paid after sale — designed to generate cash flow without the capital cost of building a large mine.
  • If proven, that cash flow could help fund the larger Los Lirios project, where EVR wants to establish a JORC resource.
  • Concept is attractive but unproven in practice — Craig frames it as one to watch for execution, not yet a confirmed thesis.
TNC Neutral FA 00:48:33
  • New assay results continue to confirm and extend mineralisation at the Aquila discovery within the broader Mount Oxide system — wider intercepts and some higher-grade sections.
  • Craig's take: "nothing earth-shattering," just incremental proof-up work needed to eventually wrap a resource around Aquila and support the long-term Mount Oxide thesis.

Session Themes

  • Repeated distinction between an attractive geological/thematic story and an investable valuation — most explicit with SRL (sector leader, government-backed, still "no value" at the current price given NPV vs. market cap).
  • Evidence-quality hierarchy matters: visual mineralisation, handheld spot readings, historical RAB drilling and scanning technology are useful indicators but are explicitly ranked below laboratory assays over defined intervals (HWK).
  • Dilution is treated as an unavoidable part of small-cap resource investing — the practical defence is entry valuation discipline and funding runway, not avoiding dilution altogether (ARO, LGM).
  • A large change in underlying technical assumptions (SPD's chromite recovery jumping from 30% to 85.6%) is a legitimate, constructive reason to delay a study, not a red flag.
  • For premium/growth non-resource names, revenue growth alone is not enough — Life360 showed why investors need to check whether costs are growing faster than revenue (no operating leverage) before trusting headline growth numbers.

Fundamental Analysis Scan with Craig Dickson

Hosted by Craig Dickson | Tuesday 11 August 2026
Bullish Setups: ILT, AVM, PER, S&M
Bearish Setups: SRL, PTN

  • New copper-bearing mineralisation appearing beneath/adjacent to the higher-grade silver veins suggests a possible broader, flatter, lower-grade copper system underneath the silver zone — added geological optionality.

PER Bullish FA 00:37:50
  • One of Craig's most interesting finds from the mid-year Gold Coast Investment Showcase; he previously held PER before a drug trial failure in 2023/24 (a normal biotech risk, not a company fault) and exited, but has been watching since.
